<FONT size=2 face="Univers,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Vanguard&#146;s Principles for Investing Success</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=2 face="Univers-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">We want to give you the best chance of investment success. These principles, grounded in Vanguard&#146;s research and experience, can put you on the right path.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=3 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Chairman&#8217;s Letter</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Dear Shareholder,</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The fiscal year ended December 31, 2015, was a tumultuous one for the world&#8217;s financial markets, and the broad U.S. stock market navigated a bumpy road to modest gains. Stocks of larger domestic companies such as those held in Vanguard 500 Index Fund generally outperformed their mid- and small-sized counterparts.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>In this investment environment, your fund returned 1.25% for Investor Shares, closely tracking its benchmark, the Standard &amp; Poor&#8217;s 500 Index, and surpassing the &#8211;0.66% average return of its peers.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Results among the fund&#8217;s ten market sectors were mixed. Half posted gains; consumer discretionary, technology, and health care stocks added most to returns. Energy stocks were a notable drag on performance.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>If you hold shares of the fund in a taxable account, you may wish to review the section on after-tax returns that appears later in this report.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Despite troubles, U.S. stocks </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>eked out a seventh year of gains</FONT><BR><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>U.S. stocks returned 0.48% for the </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>12 months ended December 31, 2015. </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Although the broad market recorded its </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>worst performance since 2008, it still </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>posted gains for the seventh straight </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>calendar year when dividends are </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>factored into returns.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>2</FONT></P></DIV>

<DIV style=" PADDING-LEFT: 0%; PADDING-RIGHT: 0%">

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Stocks rose modestly over the first half of the year but slid in August and September as concerns mounted that China&#8217;s economic slowdown would spread globally. Falling oil and commodity prices also affected economies and markets across the world for better or worse. Central banks in Europe and Asia bolstered their stimulus efforts against weak growth and low inflation. And in December, the Federal Reserve ended months of uncertainty when it raised the target for short-term interest rates to 0.25%&#8211;0.5%.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>International stocks returned about &#8211;5%, restrained by the U.S. dollar&#8217;s strength against many foreign currencies. Emerging markets fared the worst.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>U.S. bonds ended the year with a slender advance</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The broad U.S. taxable bond market gained 0.55% over the 12 months; income accounted for the modestly positive result. The yield of the 10-year Treasury note ended December at 2.30%, up from 2.19% a year earlier. (Bond prices and yields move in opposite directions.)</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Investors focused on the Fed&#8217;s stance on short-term interest rates and alternately embraced or avoided safe-haven assets depending on the stock market&#8217;s strength.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>International bond markets (as measured by the Barclays Global Aggregate Index ex USD) returned &#8211;6.02%, reduced by the</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Most segments of the U.S. economy grew, propped up by shoppers&#8217; overall confidence and their willingness and ability to spend. Internet retailers led the way in consumer discretionary; home improvement stores and restaurants also excelled. In consumer goods, notable showings came from tobacco, beverage, and packaged food companies.</FONT></P>

In IT, gains from internet and software firms were partially offset by poor results from technology hardware and communications equipment companies.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Merger-and-acquisition activity, vibrant drug pipelines, and favorable long-term demographic and economic trends lifted the health care sector. <P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Much of the contribution made by these industries was erased by a double-digit decline in energy. The lengthy and sharp slide of oil prices punished the sector. Their effect was worsened by high production levels from some leading oil-producing countries and concerns about the slower growth in China, the world&#8217;s largest oil importer.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Natural gas prices also dropped, though not as dramatically. Some integrated oil and gas firms held up better than others, but the majority of companies engaged in production and exploration as well as services and distribution suffered.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Stocks in the financial, industrials, materials, and utilities sectors also weighed on the fund&#8217;s performance.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The fund&#8217;s long-term record continues to be admirable</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Over the last ten years, Vanguard 500 Index Fund&#8217;s Investor Shares have produced an average annual return of 7.18%. That&#8217;s more than 1 percentage point better than the average return of peer funds.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Most important, the fund has succeeded in meeting its primary objective of closely tracking its index over the long-term. That was no easy feat during a period that included the worst global recession since the Great Depression. This success is a tribute to the experience, talent, and sophisticated systems of the fund&#8217;s advisor, Vanguard Equity Index Group. Low expenses&#8211;&#8211;which allow you to keep more of the fund&#8217;s return&#8212;have helped as well.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Vanguard&#8217;s outlook for investors: Not bearish, but cautious</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>In Vanguard&#8217;s recently published global economic and investment outlook, Global Chief Economist Joseph Davis and his team discuss various market and economic events 2016 may bring, along with challenges and opportunities for investors.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Our forecast includes &#8220;frustratingly fragile&#8221; economic growth and more modest long-term returns from the global stock and bond markets. The report cautions that for the decade ending 2025, returns for a balanced portfolio are likely to be moderately below historical averages.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Our simulations indicate that the average annualized returns of a 60% equity/40% bond portfolio for the decade are most likely to be centered in the 3%&#8211;5% range after inflation, below the actual average after-inflation return of 5.5% for the same portfolio since 1926.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Even so, Vanguard&#8217;s steadfast belief in its principles for investing success&#8212;focusing on clear goals, a suitable asset allocation, low costs, and long-term discipline&#8212;remains unchanged.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>For more information about our expectations and the probability of various outcomes, see</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-LightObl,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Vanguard&#8217;s Economic and Investment Outlook</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>, available at vanguard.com/research.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>To reach your long-term goals, be realistic and try to save more</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Although there have been times when it felt as if stocks and bonds were riding a roller coaster, returns have generally risen in recent years. The broad global stock market in particular has posted some impressive gains since its turnaround began in 2009.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>But 2015 served as a reminder that results aren&#8217;t always favorable. The U.S. stock and bond markets were barely positive, and international stocks and unhedged bonds finished in the red.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>In Vanguard&#8217;s recently updated long-term look at the economy and markets, our global economists explain why they expect economic growth to remain &#8220;frustratingly </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>fragile&#8221; and why their outlook for stock and bond markets is the most guarded since 2006. (For more details, see the box on page 6 and </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-LightObl,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Vanguard&#8217;s Economic and Investment Outlook</FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>, available at vanguard.com/research.)</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Given these muted expectations, what&#8217;s the best course of action? I&#8217;ve often encouraged shareholders to focus on the things they can control. That advice holds true today.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Consider saving more than you think you may need. That&#8217;s one way you can prepare for the volatility that may lie ahead, particularly as markets adjust to changes in policies from the Fed and other central banks.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Cn,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>IMPORTANT: The projections or other information generated by the Vanguard Capital Markets Model (VCMM) regarding the likelihood of various investment outcomes are hypothetical in nature, do not reflect actual investment results, and are not guarantees of future results. VCMM results will vary with each use and over time.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-LightCn,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The VCMM projections are based on a statistical analysis of historical data. Future returns may behave differently from the historical patterns captured in the VCMM. More important, the VCMM may be underestimating extreme negative scenarios unobserved in the historical period on which the model estimation is based.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-LightCn,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The VCMM is a proprietary financial simulation tool developed and maintained by Vanguard&#8217;s primary investment research and advice teams. The model forecasts distributions of future returns for a wide array of broad asset classes. Those asset classes include U.S. and international equity markets, several maturities of the U.S. Treasury and corporate fixed income markets, international fixed income markets, U.S. money markets, commodities, and certain alternative investment strategies. The theoretical and empirical foundation for the VCMM is that the returns of various asset classes reflect the compensation investors require for bearing different types of systematic risk (beta). At the core of the model are estimates of the dynamic statistical relationship between risk factors and asset returns, obtained from statistical analysis based on available monthly financial and economic data from as early as 1960. Using a system of estimated equations, the model then applies a Monte Carlo simulation method to project the estimated interrelationships among risk factors and asset classes as well as uncertainty and randomness over time. The model generates a large set of simulated outcomes for each asset class over several time horizons. Forecasts are obtained by computing measures of central tendency in these simulations. Results produced by the tool will vary with each use and over time.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>And, as always, investors would be well- </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>served to follow Vanguard&#8217;s principles for </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>investing success:</FONT><BR><BR><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>&#8226; Goals. </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Create clear, appropriate </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>investment goals.</FONT><BR><BR><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>&#8226; Balance. </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Develop a suitable asset </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>allocation using broadly diversified funds.</FONT><BR><BR><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>&#8226; Cost. </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Minimize cost.</FONT><BR><BR><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>&#8226; Discipline. </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Maintain perspective and </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>long-term discipline.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>As with saving, each of these principles is within your control, and focusing on them can keep you on the right path.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>500 Index Fund</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=3 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Notes to Financial Statements</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Vanguard 500 Index Fund is registered under the Investment Company Act of 19</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>4</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>0 as an open-end investment company, or mutual fund. The fund offers three classes of shares: Investor Shares, ETF Shares, and Admiral Shares. Investor Shares are available to any investor who meets the fund&#8217;s minimum purchase requirements. ETF Shares are listed for trading on NYSE Arca; they can be purchased and sold through a broker. Admiral Shares are designed for investors who meet certain administrative, service, and account-size criteria. Prior to October 2</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>4</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>, 201</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>4</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>, the fund offered Signal Shares. Effective at the close of business on October 2</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>4</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>, 201</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>4</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>, the Signal Shares were converted to Admiral Shares.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>A. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The following significant accounting policies conform to generally accepted accounting principles for U.S. investment companies. The fund consistently follows such policies in preparing its financial statements.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>1. Security Valuation: Securities are valued as of the close of trading on the New York Stock Exchange (generally </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>4 </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>p.m., Eastern time) on the valuation date. Equity securities are valued at the latest quoted sales prices or official closing prices taken from the primary market in which each security trades; such securities not traded on the valuation date are valued at the mean of the latest quoted bid and asked prices. Securities for which market quotations are not readily available, or whose values have been materially affected by events occurring before the fund&#8217;s pricing time but after the close of the securities&#8217; primary markets, are valued by methods deemed by the board of trustees to represent fair value. Investments in Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund are valued at that fund&#8217;s net asset value. Temporary cash investments acquired over 60 days to maturity are valued using the latest bid prices or using valuations based on a matrix system (which considers such factors as security prices, yields, maturities, and ratings), both as furnished by independent pricing services. Other temporary cash investments are valued at amortized cost, which approximates market value.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>2. Futures Contracts: The fund uses index futures contracts to a limited extent, with the objectives of maintaining full exposure to the stock market, enhancing returns, maintaining liquidity, and minimizing transaction costs. The fund may purchase futures contracts to immediately invest incoming cash in the market, or sell futures in response to cash outflows, thereby simulating a fully invested position in the underlying index while maintaining a cash balance for liquidity. The fund may seek to enhance returns by using futures contracts instead of the underlying securities when futures are believed to be priced more attractively than the underlying securities. The primary risks associated with the use of futures contracts are imperfect correlation between changes in market values of stocks held by the fund and the prices of futures contracts, and the possibility of an illiquid market. Counterparty risk involving futures is mitigated because a regulated clearinghouse is the counterparty instead of the clearing broker. To further mitigate counterparty risk, the fund trades futures contracts on an exchange, monitors the financial strength of its clearing brokers and clearinghouse, and has entered into clearing agreements with its clearing brokers. The clearinghouse imposes initial margin requirements to secure the fund&#8217;s performance and requires daily settlement of variation margin representing changes in the market value of each contract.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Futures contracts are valued at their quoted daily settlement prices. The aggregate settlement values of the contracts are not recorded in the Statement of Net Assets. Fluctuations in the value of the contracts are recorded in the Statement of Net Assets as an asset (liability) and in the Statement of Operations as unrealized appreciation (depreciation) until the contracts are closed, when they are recorded as realized futures gains (losses).</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>26</FONT></P></DIV>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>During the year ended December 31, 2015, the fund&#8217;s average investments in long and short futures contracts represented less than 1% and 0% of net assets, respectively, based on the average of aggregate settlement values at each quarter-end during the period.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>3. Federal Income Taxes: The fund intends to continue to qualify as a regulated investment company and distribute all of its taxable income. Management has analyzed the fund&#8217;s tax positions taken for all open federal income tax years (December 31, 2012&#8211;2015), and has concluded that no provision for federal income tax is required in the fund&#8217;s financial statements.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>4</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>. Distributions: Distributions to shareholders are recorded on the ex-dividend date.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>5. Securities Lending: To earn additional income, the fund lends its securities to qualified institutional borrowers. Security loans are subject to termination by the fund at any time and are required to be secured at all times by collateral in an amount at least equal to the market value of securities loaned. Daily market fluctuations could cause the value of loaned securities to be more or less than the value of the collateral received. When this occurs, the collateral is adjusted and settled on the next business day. The fund further mitigates its counterparty risk by entering into securities lending transactions only with a diverse group of prequalified counterparties, monitoring their financial strength, and entering into master securities lending agreements with its counterparties. The master securities lending agreements provide that, in the event of a counterparty&#8217;s default (including bankruptcy), the fund may terminate any loans with that borrower, determine the net amount owed, and sell or retain the collateral up to the net amount owed to the fund; however, such actions may be subject to legal proceedings. While collateral mitigates counterparty risk, in the absence of a default the fund may experience delays and costs in recovering the securities loaned. The fund invests cash collateral received in Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund, and records a liability in the Statement of Net Assets for the return of the collateral, during the period the securities are on loan. Securities lending income represents fees charged to borrowers plus income earned on invested cash collateral, less expenses associated with the loan.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>6. Credit Facility: The fund and certain other funds managed by The Vanguard Group (&#8220;Vanguard&#8221;) participate in a $3 billion committed credit facility provided by a syndicate of lenders pursuant to a credit agreement that may be renewed annually; each fund is individually liable for its borrowings, if any, under the credit facility. Borrowings may be utilized for temporary and emergency purposes, and are subject to the fund&#8217;s regulatory and contractual borrowing restrictions. The participating funds are charged administrative fees and an annual commitment fee of 0.06% of the undrawn amount of the facility; these fees are allocated to the funds based on a method approved by the fund&#8217;s board of trustees and included in Management and Administrative expenses on the fund&#8217;s Statement of Operations. Any borrowings under this facility bear interest at a rate equal to the higher of the federal funds rate or LIBOR reference rate plus an agreed-upon spread.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The fund had no borrowings outstanding at December 31, 2015, or at any time during the period then ended.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>7</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>. Other: Dividend income is recorded on the ex-dividend date. Interest income includes income distributions received from Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund and is accrued daily. Premiums and discounts on debt securities purchased are amortized and accreted, respectively, to interest income</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>C. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Various inputs may be used to determine the value of the fund&#8217;s investments. <P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Unrealized appreciation (depreciation) on open futures contracts is required to be treated as realized gain (loss) for tax purposes.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>E. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Distributions are determined on a tax basis and may differ from net investment income and realized capital gains for financial reporting purposes. Differences may be permanent or temporary. Permanent differences are reclassified among capital accounts in the financial statements to reflect their tax character. Temporary differences arise when certain items of income, expense, gain, or loss are recognized in different periods for financial statement and tax purposes. These differences will reverse at some time in the future. Differences in classification may also result from the treatment of short-term gains as ordinary income for tax purposes.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>During the year ended December 31, 2015, the fund realized $5,126,301,000 of net capital gains resulting from in-kind redemptions&#8212;in which shareholders exchanged fund shares for securities held by the fund rather than for cash. Because such gains are not taxable to the fund, and are not distributed to shareholders, they have been reclassified from accumulated net realized losses to paid-in capital.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>For tax purposes, at December 31, 2015, the fund had $</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>48</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>,966,000 of ordinary income available for distribution. The fund used capital loss carryforwards of $</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>7</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>33,52</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>4</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>,000 to offset taxable capital gains realized during the year ended December 31, 2015. At December 31, 2015, the fund had available capital losses totaling $3,192,11</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>4</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>,000 to offset future net capital gains. Of this amount, $1,</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>7</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>63,9</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>7</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>0,000 is subject to expiration on December 31, 2016. <P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=3 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>About Your Fund&#8217;s Expenses</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>As a shareholder of the fund, you incur ongoing costs, which include costs for portfolio management, administrative services, and shareholder reports (like this one), among others. Operating expenses, which are deducted from a fund&#8217;s gross income, directly reduce the investment return of the fund.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>A fund&#8217;s expenses are expressed as a percentage of its average net assets. This figure is known as the expense ratio. The following examples are intended to help you understand the ongoing costs (in dollars) of investing in your fund and to compare these costs with those of other mutual funds. The examples are based on an investment of $1,000 made at the beginning of the period shown and held for the entire period.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The accompanying table illustrates your fund&#8217;s costs in two ways:</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>&#8226; </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Based on actual fund return. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>This section helps you to estimate the actual expenses that you paid over the period. The &#8221;Ending Account Value&#8220; shown is derived from the fund&#8216;s actual return, and the third column shows the dollar amount that would have been paid by an investor who started with $1,000 in the fund. You may use the information here, together with the amount you invested, to estimate the expenses that you paid over the period.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>To do so, simply divide your account value by $1,000 (for example, an $8,600 account value divided by $1,000 = 8.6), then multiply the result by the number given for your fund under the heading &#8221;Expenses Paid During Period.&#8220;</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>&#8226; </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Based on hypothetical 5% yearly return. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>This section is intended to help you compare your fund&#8216;s costs with those of other mutual funds. It assumes that the fund had a yearly return of 5% before expenses, but that the expense ratio is unchanged. In this case&#8212;because the return used is not the fund&#8217;s actual return&#8212;the results do not apply to your investment. The example is useful in making comparisons because the Securities and Exchange Commission requires all mutual funds to calculate expenses based on a 5% return. You can assess your fund&#8217;s costs by comparing this hypothetical example with the hypothetical examples that appear in shareholder reports of other funds.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Univers-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Note that the expenses shown in the table are meant to highlight and help you compare </FONT><I><FONT size=1 face=Univers-LightOblique,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>ongoing </FONT></I><FONT size=1 face=Univers-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>costs only and do not reflect transaction costs incurred by the fund for buying and selling securities. Further, the expenses do not include any purchase, redemption, or account service fees described in the fund prospectus. If such fees were applied to your account, your costs would be higher. Your fund does not carry a &#8220;sales load.&#8221;</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The calculations assume no shares were bought or sold during the period. Your actual costs may have been higher or lower, depending on the amount of your investment and the timing of any purchases or redemptions.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>You can find more information about the fund&#8217;s expenses, including annual expense ratios, in the Financial Statements section of this report. For additional information on operating expenses and other shareholder costs, please refer to your fund&#8217;s current prospectus.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=3 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Glossary</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>30-Day SEC Yield. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>A fund&#8217;s 30-day SEC yield is derived using a formula specified by the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission. Under the formula, data related to the fund&#8217;s security holdings in the previous 30 days are used to calculate the fund&#8217;s hypothetical net income for that period, which is then annualized and divided by the fund&#8217;s estimated average net assets over the calculation period. For the purposes of this calculation, a security&#8217;s income is based on its current market yield to maturity (for bonds), its actual income (for asset-backed securities), or its projected dividend yield (for stocks). Because the SEC yield represents hypothetical annualized income, it will differ&#8212;at times significantly&#8212;from the fund&#8217;s actual experience. As a result, the fund&#8217;s income distributions may be higher or lower than implied by the SEC yield.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Beta. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>A measure of the magnitude of a fund&#8217;s past share-price fluctuations in relation to the ups and downs of a given market index. The index is assigned a beta of 1.00. Compared with a given index, a fund with a beta of 1.20 typically would have seen its share price rise or fall by 12% when the index rose or fell by 10%. For this report, beta is based on returns over the past 36 months for both the fund and the index. Note that a fund&#8217;s beta should be reviewed in conjunction with its R-squared (see definition). The lower the R-squared, the less correlation there is between the fund and the index, and the less reliable beta is as an indicator of volatility.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Dividend Yield. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Dividend income earned by stocks, expressed as a percentage of the aggregate market value (or of net asset value, for a fund). The yield is determined by dividing the amount of the annual dividends by the aggregate value (or net asset value) at the end of the period. For a fund, the dividend yield is based solely on stock holdings and does not include any income produced by other investments.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Earnings Growth Rate. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The average annual rate of growth in earnings over the past five years for the stocks now in a fund.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Equity Exposure. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>A measure that reflects a fund&#8217;s investments in stocks and stock futures. Any holdings in short-term reserves are excluded.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Expense Ratio. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>A fund&#8217;s total annual operating expenses expressed as a percentage of the fund&#8217;s average net assets. The expense ratio includes management and administrative expenses, but does not include the transaction costs of buying and selling portfolio securities.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Foreign Holdings. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The percentage of a fund represented by securities or depositary receipts of companies based outside the United States.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Inception Date. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The date on which the assets of a fund (or one of its share classes) are first invested in accordance with the fund&#8217;s investment objective. For funds with a subscription period, the inception date is the day after that period ends. Investment performance is measured from the inception date.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Median Market Cap. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>An indicator of the size of companies in which a fund invests; the midpoint of market capitalization (market price x shares outstanding) of a fund&#8217;s stocks, weighted by the proportion of the fund&#8217;s assets invested in each stock. Stocks representing half of the fund&#8217;s assets have market capitalizations above the median, and the rest are below it.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Price/Book Ratio. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The share price of a stock divided by its net worth, or book value, per share. For a fund, the weighted average price/book ratio of the stocks it holds.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>35</FONT></P></DIV>

<DIV style="PAGE-BREAK-BEFORE: always">&nbsp;</DIV>

<!--$$/page=--><A name="page_39"></A><BR>

<DIV style=" PADDING-LEFT: 0%; PADDING-RIGHT: 0%">

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Price/Earnings Ratio. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The ratio of a stock&#8217;s current price to its per-share earnings over the past year. For a fund, the weighted average P/E of the stocks it holds. P/E is an indicator of market expectations about corporate prospects; the higher the P/E, the greater the expectations for a company&#8217;s future growth.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>R-Squared. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>A measure of how much of a fund&#8217;s past returns can be explained by the returns from the market in general, as measured by a given index. If a fund&#8217;s total returns were precisely synchronized with an index&#8217;s returns, its R-squared would be 1.00. If the fund&#8217;s returns bore no relationship to the index&#8217;s returns, its R-squared would be 0. For this report, R-squared is based on returns over the past 36 months for both the fund and the index.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Return on Equity. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The annual average rate of return generated by a company during the past five years for each dollar of shareholder&#8217;s equity (net income divided by shareholder&#8217;s equity). For a fund, the weighted average return on equity for the companies whose stocks it holds.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Short-Term Reserves. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The percentage of a fund invested in highly liquid, short-term securities that can be readily converted to cash.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Turnover Rate. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>An indication of the fund&#8217;s trading activity. Funds with high turnover rates incur higher transaction costs and may be more likely to distribute capital gains (which may be taxable to investors). The turnover rate excludes in-kind transactions, which have minimal impact on costs.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>36</FONT></P></DIV>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=Univers,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Vanguard&#8217;s Principles for Investing Success</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=Univers-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>We want to give you the best chance of investment success. These principles, grounded in Vanguard&#8217;s research and experience, can put you on the right path.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Goals. </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Create clear, appropriate investment goals.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Balance. </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Develop a suitable asset allocation using broadly diversified funds. </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Cost. </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Minimize cost.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Discipline. </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Maintain perspective and long-term discipline.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=Univers-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>A single theme unites these principles: Focus on the things you can control.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=Univers-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>We believe there is no wiser course for any investor.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: center"><FONT size=3 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif></FONT>&nbsp;</P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: center"><FONT size=3 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif></FONT>&nbsp;</P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: center"><FONT size=3 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif></FONT>&nbsp;</P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: center"><FONT size=3 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif></FONT>&nbsp;</P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=3 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Chairman&#8217;s Letter</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Dear Shareholder,</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>After three straight years of double-digit returns, the broad U.S. stock market limped to results of less than 1 percent for the 12 months ended December 31, 2015. Small-capitalization stocks fared worse: They finished in negative territory, well behind their large-cap counterparts, as investors became more risk-averse in the uncertain environment. It was their worst annual performance since 2008.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Vanguard&#8217;s three small-cap U.S. index funds recorded returns that ranged from &#8211;4.78% for the Vanguard Small-Cap Value Index Fund to &#8211;2.64% for the Vanguard Small-Cap Growth Index Fund. The broader-based Vanguard Small-Cap Index Fund, which includes both growth and value stocks, fell in between, with a return of &#8211;3.78%. (All returns are for Investor Shares.)</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>All three funds closely tracked their target indexes. Although it is not the funds&#8217; objective to outperform funds that invest in similar stocks, the Small-Cap Index Fund and Small-Cap Value Index Fund surpassed the average return of their peers. The Small-Cap Growth Index Fund trailed its comparable industry average by less than 1 percentage point.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>If you hold any of these funds in a taxable account, you may wish to review the discussion of after-tax returns that appears later in this report.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>4</FONT></P></DIV>

<DIV style="PAGE-BREAK-BEFORE: always">&nbsp;</DIV>

<!--$$/page=--><A name="page_52"></A><BR>

<DIV style="PADDING-LEFT: 0%; PADDING-RIGHT: 0%">

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Despite troubles, U.S. stocks </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>eked out a seventh year of gains</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>U.S. stocks returned 0.48% for the 12 months. Although the broad market recorded its worst performance since 2008, it still posted gains for the seventh straight calendar year when dividends are factored into returns.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Stocks rose modestly over the first half of the year but slid in August and September as concerns mounted that China&#8217;s economic slowdown would spread globally. Falling oil and commodity prices also affected economies and markets across the world for better or worse. Central banks in Europe and Asia bolstered their stimulus efforts against weak growth and low inflation. And in</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>December, the Federal Reserve ended months of uncertainty when it raised the target for short-term interest rates to 0.25%&#8211;0.5%.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>International stocks returned about &#8211;5%, restrained by the U.S. dollar&#8217;s strength against many foreign currencies. Emerging markets fared the worst.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><STRONG><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>U.S. bonds ended the year </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>with a slender advance</FONT></STRONG><BR><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The broad U.S. taxable bond market </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>gained 0.55% over the 12 months; income accounted for the modestly positive result. The yield of the 10-year Treasury note ended December at 2.30%, up from 2.19% a year earlier. (Bond prices and yields move in opposite directions.)</FONT></P>

<DIV style="PADDING-LEFT: 0%; PADDING-RIGHT: 0%">

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Investors focused on the Fed&#8217;s stance on short-term interest rates and alternately embraced or avoided safe-haven assets depending on the stock market&#8217;s strength.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>International bond markets (as measured by the Barclays Global Aggregate Index ex USD) returned &#8211;6.02%, reduced by the dollar&#8217;s strength. Without this currency effect, returns were modestly positive.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Although the Fed raised its target for short-term interest rates in mid-December, returns for money market funds and savings accounts remained limited by the 0%&#8211;0.25% levels in place for much of the past seven years.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><STRONG><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Small-cap stocks lagged </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>in challenging markets</FONT><BR></STRONG><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Small-cap stocks, which make up about </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>10% of the broad U.S. market, provide investors with both opportunities and challenges. Small companies generally have greater potential for growth than larger ones. They&#8217;re often younger and nimbler and can sometimes find a market niche or capitalize on a market trend that leads to a surge in profits. At the same time, small companies are usually more vulnerable to setbacks; they don&#8217;t benefit from the diversification of business lines or the resources and cash reserves of larger firms.</FONT></P>

<DIV style="PAGE-BREAK-BEFORE: always">&nbsp;</DIV>

<!--$$/page=--><A name="page_54"></A><BR>

<DIV style="PADDING-LEFT: 0%; PADDING-RIGHT: 0%">

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>When broader markets are unsettled, investors have traditionally favored the relative safety provided by larger, more established companies, whose results tend to be more predictable and less volatile. Small-caps, which led large-caps in cumulative return through the first six years after the financial crisis, lost their momentum amid the 2015 market weakness.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The difficulties were most apparent among oil and gas stocks, which sank 30% or more in all three funds. The sharp slide of oil prices punished the sector, in part because of high production levels</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>from some leading oil-producing countries and concerns about the slower growth in China, the world&#8217;s largest oil importer. Companies engaged in production and exploration and services and distribution all suffered.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Commodity prices also fell, hurting stocks in the funds&#8217; basic materials sector, including metals and mining, forestry and paper, and chemical businesses. Results were also negative in the consumer goods, consumer services, industrials, and telecommunications sectors, although the declines weren&#8217;t always as glaring.</FONT></P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0px">&nbsp;</P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The figures shown represent past performance, which is not a guarantee of future results. (Current performance may be lower or higher than the performance data cited. For performance data current to the most recent month-end, visit our website at vanguard.com/performance.) Note, too, that both investment returns and principal value can fluctuate widely, so an investor&#8217;s shares, when sold, could be worth more or less than their original cost.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>7</FONT></P></DIV>

<DIV style="PAGE-BREAK-BEFORE: always">&nbsp;</DIV>

<!--$$/page=--><A name="page_55"></A><BR>

<DIV style=" PADDING-LEFT: 0%; PADDING-RIGHT: 0%">

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Health care and technology, two traditional growth-oriented sectors, led returns for the Small-Cap Index Fund and the Growth Index Fund. Long-term demographic and economic trends continue to propel health care stocks, and merger-and-acquisition activity and robust drug pipelines also lent a boost. Still, returns for the sector didn&#8217;t compare with those of recent years, as the lofty valuations of biotechnology stocks and controversy over high drug prices rattled investors at times.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Technology stocks produced muted gains, but results fluctuated across the sector&#8217;s business segments. Leaders</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>included software and service firms that differentiated themselves in the marketplace, delivered innovative products and solutions, and capitalized on the continued shift to mobile and cloud computing.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Financials, the largest sector for all three funds, reflected the overall sluggishness that enveloped both the broader and small-cap markets. Banks&#8212;which stand to benefit from the increase in short-term interest rates&#8212;and insurance companies carried the sector; asset managers, consumer finance firms, and mortgage companies had a rougher time.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Vanguard&#8217;s outlook for investors: Not bearish, but cautious</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>In Vanguard&#8217;s recently published global economic and investment outlook, Global Chief Economist Joseph Davis and his team discuss various market and economic events 2016 may bring, along with challenges and opportunities for investors.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Our forecast includes &#8220;frustratingly fragile&#8221; economic growth and more modest long-term returns from the global stock and bond markets. The report cautions that for the decade ending 2025, returns for a balanced portfolio are likely to be moderately below historical averages.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Our simulations indicate that the average annualized returns of a 60% equity/40% bond portfolio for the decade are most likely to be centered in the 3%&#8211;5% range after inflation, below the actual average after-inflation return of 5.5% for the same portfolio since 1926.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Even so, Vanguard&#8217;s steadfast belief in its principles for investing success&#8212;focusing on clear goals, a suitable asset allocation, low costs, and long-term discipline&#8212;remains unchanged.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>For more information about our expectations and the probability of various outcomes, see</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-LightObl,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Vanguard&#8217;s Economic and Investment Outlook</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>, available at vanguard.com/research.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Cn,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>IMPORTANT: The projections or other information generated by the Vanguard Capital Markets Model</FONT><SUP><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Cn,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>&#174; </FONT></SUP><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Cn,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>(VCMM) regarding the likelihood of various investment outcomes are hypothetical in nature, do not reflect actual investment results, and are not guarantees of future results. Distribution of return outcomes from VCMM, derived from 10,000 simulations for U.S. equity returns and fixed income returns. Simulations as of September 30, 2015. Results from the model may vary with each use and over time. For more information, please see page 9.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>8</FONT></P></DIV>

<DIV style="PAGE-BREAK-BEFORE: always">&nbsp;</DIV>

<!--$$/page=--><A name="page_56"></A><BR>

<DIV style=" PADDING-LEFT: 0%; PADDING-RIGHT: 0%">

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>All three small-cap index funds </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>tightly tracked their benchmarks</FONT><BR><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>For the decade ended December 31, </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>2015, each of the three small-cap index funds generated an average annual return of more than 7%. Most important, all three funds met their primary objective of tightly tracking their benchmark returns over a volatile period that included the worst bear market in 75 years and the subsequent recovery.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Index tracking may appear simple from the outside, but it requires sophisticated trading and portfolio construction techniques. The funds&#8217; success in tracking their indexes is a testament to the expertise and experience of their advisor, Vanguard Equity Index Group.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Additionally, over the decade, all three funds topped the average annual returns of their peer funds, many of which are</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>actively managed. The Small-Cap Index Fund&#8217;s return was 2 percentage points ahead of its peer average, and the other two funds surpassed their peers by more than 1 percentage point.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>To reach your long-term goals, </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>be realistic and try to save more</FONT><BR><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Although there have been times when it </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>felt as if stocks and bonds were riding a roller coaster, the markets have generally risen in recent years. The broad global stock market in particular has posted some impressive gains since its turnaround began in 2009.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>But 2015 served as a reminder that markets aren&#8217;t always favorable. The U.S. stock and bond markets were barely positive, and international stocks and unhedged bonds finished in the red.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Cn,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>IMPORTANT: The projections or other information generated by the Vanguard Capital Markets Model (VCMM) regarding the likelihood of various investment outcomes are hypothetical in nature, do not reflect actual investment results, and are not guarantees of future results. VCMM results will vary with each use and over time.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-LightCn,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The VCMM projections are based on a statistical analysis of historical data. Future returns may behave differently from the historical patterns captured in the VCMM. More important, the VCMM may be underestimating extreme negative scenarios unobserved in the historical period on which the model estimation is based.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-LightCn,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The VCMM is a proprietary financial simulation tool developed and maintained by Vanguard&#8217;s primary investment research and advice teams. The model forecasts distributions of future returns for a wide array of broad asset classes. Those asset classes include U.S. and international equity markets, several maturities of the U.S. Treasury and corporate fixed income markets, international fixed income markets, U.S. money markets, commodities, and certain alternative investment strategies. The theoretical and empirical foundation for the VCMM is that the returns of various asset classes reflect the compensation investors require for bearing different types of systematic risk (beta). At the core of the model are estimates of the dynamic statistical relationship between risk factors and asset returns, obtained from statistical analysis based on available monthly financial and economic data from as early as 1960. Using a system of estimated equations, the model then applies a Monte Carlo simulation method to project the estimated interrelationships among risk factors and asset classes as well as uncertainty and randomness over time. The model generates a large set of simulated outcomes for each asset class over several time horizons. Forecasts are obtained by computing measures of central tendency in these simulations. Results produced by the tool will vary with each use and over time.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>9</FONT></P></DIV>

<DIV style="PAGE-BREAK-BEFORE: always">&nbsp;</DIV>

<!--$$/page=--><A name="page_57"></A><BR>

<DIV style="PADDING-LEFT: 0%; PADDING-RIGHT: 0%">

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>In Vanguard&#8217;s recently updated long-term look at the economy and markets, our global economists explain why they expect economic growth to remain &#8220;frustratingly fragile,&#8221; and why their outlook for stock and bond markets is the most guarded since 2006. (For more details, see the box on page 8 and </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-LightObl,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Vanguard&#8217;s Economic and Investment Outlook</FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>, available at vanguard.com/research.)</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Given these muted expectations, what&#8217;s the best course of action? I&#8217;ve often encouraged shareholders to focus on the things they can control. That advice holds true today.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Consider saving more than you think you may need. That&#8217;s one way you can prepare for the volatility that may lie ahead, particularly as markets adjust to changes in policies from the Fed and other central banks.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>And, as always, investors would be well-</FONT><BR><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>served to follow Vanguard&#8217;s principles</FONT><BR><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>for investing success:</FONT><BR><BR><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>&#8226; Goals. </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Create clear, appropriate </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>investment goals.</FONT><BR><BR><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>&#8226; Balance. </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Develop a suitable asset </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>allocation using broadly diversified funds.</FONT><BR><BR><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>&#8226; Cost. </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Minimize cost.</FONT><BR><BR><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>&#8226; Discipline. </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Maintain perspective and </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>long-term discipline.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>As with saving, each of these principles is within your control, and focusing on them can keep you on the right path.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>As always, thank you for investing with Vanguard.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Small-Cap Index Fund</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=3 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Notes to Financial Statements</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Vanguard Small-Cap Index Fund is registered under the Investment Company Act of 19</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>4</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>0 as an open-end investment company, or mutual fund. The fund offers five classes of shares: Investor Shares, ETF Shares, Admiral Shares, Institutional Shares, and Institutional Plus Shares. Investor Shares are available to any investor who meets the fund&#8217;s minimum purchase requirements. ETF Shares are listed for trading on NYSE Arca; they can be purchased and sold through a broker. Admiral Shares, Institutional Shares, and Institutional Plus Shares are designed for investors who meet certain administrative, service, and account-size criteria. Prior to October 2</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>4</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>, 201</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>4</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>, the fund offered Signal Shares. Effective October 2</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>4</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>, 201</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>4</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>, the Signal Shares were converted to Admiral Shares.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>A. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The following significant accounting policies conform to generally accepted accounting principles for U.S. investment companies. The fund consistently follows such policies in preparing its financial statements.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>1. Security Valuation: Securities are valued as of the close of trading on the New York Stock Exchange (generally </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>4 </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>p.m., Eastern time) on the valuation date. Equity securities are valued at the latest quoted sales prices or official closing prices taken from the primary market in which each security trades; such securities not traded on the valuation date are valued at the mean of the latest quoted bid and asked prices. Securities for which market quotations are not readily available, or whose values have been materially affected by events occurring before the fund&#8217;s pricing time but after the close of the securities&#8217; primary markets, are valued by methods deemed by the board of trustees to represent fair value. Investments in Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund are valued at that fund&#8217;s net asset value. Temporary cash investments acquired over 60 days to maturity are valued using the latest bid prices or using valuations based on a matrix system (which considers such factors as security prices, yields, maturities, and ratings), both as furnished by independent pricing services. Other temporary cash investments are valued at amortized cost, which approximates market value.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>2. Futures Contracts: The fund uses index futures contracts to a limited extent, with the objectives of maintaining full exposure to the stock market, enhancing returns, maintaining liquidity, and minimizing transaction costs. The fund may purchase futures contracts to immediately invest incoming cash in the market, or sell futures in response to cash outflows, thereby simulating a fully invested position in the underlying index while maintaining a cash balance for liquidity. The fund may seek to enhance returns by using futures contracts instead of the underlying securities when futures are believed to be priced more attractively than the underlying securities. The primary risks associated with the use of futures contracts are imperfect correlation between changes in market values of stocks held by the fund and the prices of futures contracts, and the possibility of an illiquid market. Counterparty risk involving futures is mitigated because a regulated clearinghouse is the counterparty instead of the clearing broker. To further mitigate counterparty risk, the fund trades futures contracts on an exchange, monitors the financial strength of its clearing brokers and clearinghouse, and has entered into clearing agreements with its clearing brokers. The clearinghouse imposes initial margin requirements to secure the fund&#8217;s performance and requires daily settlement of variation margin representing changes in the market value of each contract.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Futures contracts are valued at their quoted daily settlement prices. The aggregate settlement values of the contracts are not recorded in the Statement of Net Assets. Fluctuations in the value of the contracts are recorded in the Statement of Net Assets as an asset (liability) and in the Statement of Operations as unrealized appreciation (depreciation) until the contracts are closed, when they are recorded as realized futures gains (losses).</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>27</FONT></P></DIV>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Small-Cap Index Fund</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>During the year ended December 31, 2015, the fund&#8217;s average investments in long and short futures contracts represented less than 1% and 0% of net assets, respectively, based on the average of aggregate settlement values at each quarter-end during the period.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>3. Swap Contracts: The fund has entered into equity swap contracts to earn the total return on selected reference stocks in the fund&#8217;s target index. Under the terms of the swaps, the fund receives the total return on the referenced stock (i.e., receiving the increase or paying the decrease in value of the selected reference stock and receiving the equivalent of any dividends in respect of the selected referenced stock) over a specified period of time, applied to a notional amount that represents the value of a designated number of shares of the selected reference stock at the beginning of the equity swap contract. The fund also pays a floating rate that is based on short-term interest rates, applied to the notional amount. At the same time, the fund invests an amount approximating the notional amount of the swap in high-quality temporary cash investments.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The notional amounts of swap contracts are not recorded in the Statement of Net Assets. Swaps are valued daily based on market quotations received from independent pricing services or recognized dealers and the change in value is recorded in the Statement of Net Assets as an asset (liability) and in the Statement of Operations as unrealized appreciation (depreciation) until termination of the swap, at which time realized gain (loss) is recorded. A risk associated with all types of swaps is the possibility that a counterparty may default on its obligation to pay net amounts due to the fund. The fund&#8217;s maximum amount subject to counterparty risk is the unrealized appreciation on the swap contract. The fund mitigates its counterparty risk by entering into swaps only with a diverse group of prequalified counterparties, monitoring their financial strength, entering into master netting arrangements with its counterparties, and requiring its counterparties to transfer collateral as security for their performance. In the event of a counterparty&#8217;s default (including bankruptcy), the fund may terminate any swap contracts with that counterparty, determine the net amount owed by either party in accordance with its master netting arrangements, and sell or retain any collateral held up to the net amount owed to the fund under the master netting arrangements. The swap contracts contain provisions whereby a counterparty may terminate open contracts if the fund net assets decline below a certain level, triggering a payment by the fund if the fund is in a net liability position at the time of the termination. The payment amount would be reduced by any collateral the fund has pledged. Any securities pledged as collateral for open contracts are noted in the Statement of Net Assets. The value of collateral received or pledged is compared daily to the value of the swap contracts exposure with each counterparty, and any difference, if in excess of a specified minimum transfer amount, is adjusted and settled within two business days.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>During the year ended December 31, 2015, the fund&#8217;s average amounts of investments in total return swaps represented less than 1% of net assets, based on the average of notional amounts at each quarter-end during the period.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>4</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>. Federal Income Taxes: The fund intends to continue to qualify as a regulated investment company and distribute all of its taxable income. Management has analyzed the fund&#8217;s tax positions taken for all open federal income tax years (December 31, 2012&#8211;2015), and has concluded that no provision for federal income tax is required in the fund&#8217;s financial statements.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>5. Distributions: Distributions to shareholders are recorded on the ex-dividend date.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>28</FONT></P></DIV>
