<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=3 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Chairman&#8217;s Letter</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Dear Shareholder,</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The year ended December 31, 2015, was a tumultuous one for the world&#8217;s financial markets. Not immune to the volatility, the broad U.S. stock market navigated a bumpy road to modest gains. Growth stocks outpaced their value counterparts, while large-capitalization stocks exceeded mid-caps and small-caps.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>In this investment environment, Vanguard&#8217;s three large-capitalization U.S. index funds produced varying results. Vanguard Growth Index Fund returned 3.17%, while Vanguard Value Index Fund returned &#8211;1.03%. Vanguard Large-Cap Index Fund, which holds both growth and value stocks, returned 0.93%. (All returns are for the funds&#8217; Investor Shares.) Each fund closely tracked its target index for the fiscal year.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>If you hold any of these funds in a taxable account, you may wish to review the table of after-tax returns that appears later in this report.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Despite troubles, U.S. stocks </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>eked out a seventh year of gains</FONT><BR><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>U.S. stocks returned 0.48% for the 12 </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>months ended December 31, 2015. </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Although the broad market recorded its </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>worst performance since 2008, it still </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>posted gains for the seventh straight </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>calendar year when dividends are </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>factored into returns.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>4</FONT></P></DIV>

<DIV style="PAGE-BREAK-BEFORE: always">&nbsp;</DIV>

<!--$$/page=--><A name="page_244"></A><BR>

<DIV style=" PADDING-LEFT: 0%; PADDING-RIGHT: 0%">

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Stocks rose modestly over the first half of the year but slid in August and September as concerns mounted that China&#8217;s economic slowdown would spread globally. Falling oil and commodity prices also affected economies and markets across the world for better or worse. Central banks in Europe and Asia bolstered their stimulus efforts against weak growth and low inflation. And in December, the Federal Reserve ended months of uncertainty when it raised the target for short-term interest rates to 0.25%&#8211;0.5%.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>International stocks returned about &#8211;5%, restrained by the U.S. dollar&#8217;s strength against many foreign currencies. Emerging markets fared the worst.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>U.S. bonds ended the year with a slender advance</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The broad U.S. taxable bond market gained 0.55% over the 12 months; income accounted for the modestly positive result. The yield of the 10-year Treasury note ended December at 2.30%, up from 2.19% a year earlier. (Bond prices and yields move in opposite directions.)</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Investors focused on the Fed&#8217;s stance on short-term interest rates and alternately embraced or avoided safe-haven assets depending on the stock market&#8217;s strength.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>International bond markets (as measured by the Barclays Global Aggregate Index ex USD) returned &#8211;6.02%, reduced by</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Although the Fed raised its target for short-term interest rates in mid-December, returns for money market funds and savings accounts remained limited by the 0%&#8211;0.25% levels in place for much of the past seven years.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Gains in some sectors were offset by energy&#8217;s double-digit decline</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Vanguard&#8217;s three large-cap index funds provide exposure to some of the United States&#8217; biggest companies. Investors can invest broadly in the large-cap market through the Large-Cap Index Fund, or </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>focus specifically on large-cap growth or value stocks through one of the other two funds.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>As I mentioned earlier, growth stocks trumped their value counterparts for the 12 months. The performance of Vanguard&#8217;s large-cap index funds mirrored this broad market trend, with the Growth Index Fund outpacing the Value Index Fund by several percentage points. Results by sector were mixed, and the performance of a few sectors varied between the funds.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>For the most part the U.S. economy grew, boosted by shoppers&#8217; overall confidence and their willingness and ability to spend. This trend benefited the consumer</FONT></P>

For the fiscal year ended December 31, 2015, the funds&#8217; expense ratios were: for the Growth Index Fund, 0.22% for Investor Shares, 0.08% for ETF Shares, 0.08% for Admiral Shares, and 0.07% for Institutional Shares; for the Value Index Fund, 0.22% for Investor Shares, 0.08% for ETF Shares, 0.08% for Admiral Shares, and 0.07% for Institutional Shares; and for the Large-Cap Index Fund, 0.20% for Investor Shares, 0.08% for ETF Shares, 0.08% for Admiral Shares, and 0.07% for Institutional Shares. The peer-group expense ratios are derived from data provided by Lipper, a Thomson Reuters Company, and capture information through year-end 2014.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>services and consumer goods sectors. Consumer services was the top performer in both the Growth Index Fund and the Large-Cap Index Fund, with internet retailers, home improvement stores, and restaurants generally leading the way. (The sector posted a negative result for the Value Index Fund.) Within the consumer goods sector, tobacco and beverage companies did very well in each of the three funds.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Gains in the information technology and health care sectors also helped the funds&#8217; performance; however, returns for both </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>paled compared with those seen in some recent periods. The tiny telecommunications sector also posted a positive result for each fund.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Much of the contribution made by these sectors was erased by a double-digit decline in oil and gas, which was the most significant detractor in all three funds by a wide margin. The lengthy and sharp slide of oil prices punished the sector, in part because of high production levels from some leading oil-producing countries and concerns about the slower growth in China, the world&#8217;s largest oil importer. <P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=2 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">included the worst global recession since the Great Depression. That they did so is a tribute to the experience, talent, and sophisticated systems of their advisor, Vanguard Equity Index Group. The funds&#146; low expenses&#150;&#150;which allow you to keep more of the return on your investment&#150;&#150;have helped in these efforts.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=2 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">To reach your long-term goals, be realistic and try to save more</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=2 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Although there have been times when it felt as if stocks and bonds were riding a roller coaster, the markets have generally risen in recent years. The broad global stock market in particular has posted some impressive gains since its turnaround began in 2009.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=2 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">But 2015 served as a reminder that markets aren&#146;t always favorable. The U.S. stock and bond markets were basically flat, and international stocks and unhedged bonds finished in the red.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=2 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">In Vanguard&#146;s recently updated long-term look at the economy and markets, our global economists explain why they expect economic growth to remain &#147;frustratingly fragile,&#148; and why their outlook for stock and bond markets is the most guarded since 2006. (For more details, see the box on page 8 and </FONT><FONT size=2 face="UniversLTStd-LightObl,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Vanguard&#146;s Economic and Investment Outlook</FONT><FONT size=2 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">, available at vanguard.com/research.)</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-Cn,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">IMPORTANT: The projections or other information generated by the Vanguard Capital Markets Model (VCMM) regarding the likelihood of various investment outcomes are hypothetical in nature, do not reflect actual investment results, and are not guarantees of future results. VCMM results will vary with each use and over time.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-LightCn,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">The VCMM projections are based on a statistical analysis of historical data. Future returns may behave differently from the historical patterns captured in the VCMM. More important, the VCMM may be underestimating extreme negative scenarios unobserved in the historical period on which the model estimation is based.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=1 face="UniversLTStd-LightCn,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">The VCMM is a proprietary financial simulation tool developed and maintained by Vanguard&#146;s primary investment research and advice teams. The model forecasts distributions of future returns for a wide array of broad asset classes. Those asset classes include U.S. and international equity markets, several maturities of the U.S. Treasury and corporate fixed income markets, international fixed income markets, U.S. money markets, commodities, and certain alternative investment strategies. The theoretical and empirical foundation for the VCMM is that the returns of various asset classes reflect the compensation investors require for bearing different types of systematic risk (beta). At the core of the model are estimates of the dynamic statistical relationship between risk factors and asset returns, obtained from statistical analysis based on available monthly financial and economic data from as early as 1960. Using a system of estimated equations, the model then applies a Monte Carlo simulation method to project the estimated interrelationships among risk factors and asset classes as well as uncertainty and randomness over time. The model generates a large set of simulated outcomes for each asset class over several time horizons. Forecasts are obtained by computing measures of central tendency in these simulations. Results produced by the tool will vary with each use and over time.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Given these muted expectations, what&#8217;s the best course of action? I&#8217;ve often encouraged shareholders to focus on the things they can control. That advice holds true today.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Consider saving more than you think you may need. That&#8217;s one way you can prepare for the volatility that may lie ahead, particularly as markets adjust to changes in policies from the Fed and other central banks.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>And, as always, investors would be well-served to follow Vanguard&#8217;s principles for investing success:</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>&#8226; Goals. </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Create clear, appropriate investment goals.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>&#8226; Balance. </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Develop a suitable asset allocation using broadly diversified funds.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>&#8226; Cost. </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Minimize cost.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>&#8226; Discipline. </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Maintain perspective and long-term discipline.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>As with saving, each of these principles is within your control, and focusing on them can keep you on the right path.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Growth Index Fund</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=3 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Notes to Financial Statements</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Vanguard Growth Index Fund is registered under the Investment Company Act of 19</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>4</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>0 as an open-end investment company, or mutual fund. The fund offers four classes of shares: Investor Shares, ETF Shares, Admiral Shares, and Institutional Shares. Investor Shares are available to any investor who meets the fund&#8217;s minimum purchase requirements. ETF Shares are listed for trading on NYSE Arca; they can be purchased and sold through a broker. Admiral Shares and Institutional Shares are designed for investors who meet certain administrative, service, and account-size criteria. Prior to October 2</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>4</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>, 201</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>4</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>, the fund offered Signal Shares. Effective at the close of business on October 2</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>4</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>, 201</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>4</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>, the Signal Shares were converted to Admiral Shares.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>A. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The following significant accounting policies conform to generally accepted accounting principles for U.S. investment companies. The fund consistently follows such policies in preparing its financial statements.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>1. Security Valuation: Securities are valued as of the close of trading on the New York Stock Exchange (generally </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>4 </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>p.m., Eastern time) on the valuation date. Equity securities are valued at the latest quoted sales prices or official closing prices taken from the primary market in which each security trades; such securities not traded on the valuation date are valued at the mean of the latest quoted bid and asked prices. Securities for which market quotations are not readily available, or whose values have been materially affected by events occurring before the fund&#8217;s pricing time but after the close of the securities&#8217; primary markets, are valued by methods deemed by the board of trustees to represent fair value. Investments in Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund are valued at that fund&#8217;s net asset value. Temporary cash investments acquired over 60 days to maturity are valued using the latest bid prices or using valuations based on a matrix system (which considers such factors as security prices, yields, maturities, and ratings), both as furnished by independent pricing services. Other temporary cash investments are valued at amortized cost, which approximates market value.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>2. Futures Contracts: The fund uses index futures contracts to a limited extent, with the objectives of maintaining full exposure to the stock market, enhancing returns, maintaining liquidity, and minimizing transaction costs. The fund may purchase futures contracts to immediately invest incoming cash in the market, or sell futures in response to cash outflows, thereby simulating a fully invested position in the underlying index while maintaining a cash balance for liquidity. The fund may seek to enhance returns by using futures contracts instead of the underlying securities when futures are believed to be priced more attractively than the underlying securities. The primary risks associated with the use of futures contracts are imperfect correlation between changes in market values of stocks held by the fund and the prices of futures contracts, and the possibility of an illiquid market. Counterparty risk involving futures is mitigated because a regulated clearinghouse is the counterparty instead of the clearing broker. To further mitigate counterparty risk, the fund trades futures contracts on an exchange, monitors the financial strength of its clearing brokers and clearinghouse, and has entered into clearing agreements with its clearing brokers. The clearinghouse imposes initial margin requirements to secure the fund&#8217;s performance and requires daily settlement of variation margin representing changes in the market value of each contract.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Futures contracts are valued at their quoted daily settlement prices. The aggregate settlement values of the contracts are not recorded in the Statement of Net Assets. Fluctuations in the value of the contracts are recorded in the Statement of Net Assets as an asset (liability) and in the Statement of Operations as unrealized appreciation (depreciation) until the contracts are closed, when they are recorded as realized futures gains (losses).</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>27</FONT></P></DIV>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Growth Index Fund</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>During the year ended December 31, 2015, the fund&#8217;s average investments in long and short futures contracts represented less than 1% and 0% of net assets, respectively, based on the average of aggregate settlement values at each quarter-end during the period.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>3. Federal Income Taxes: The fund intends to continue to qualify as a regulated investment company and distribute all of its taxable income. Management has analyzed the fund&#8217;s tax positions taken for all open federal income tax years (December 31, 2012&#8211;2015), and has concluded that no provision for federal income tax is required in the fund&#8217;s financial statements.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>4</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>. Distributions: Distributions to shareholders are recorded on the ex-dividend date.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>5. Securities Lending: To earn additional income, the fund lends its securities to qualified institutional borrowers. Security loans are subject to termination by the fund at any time and are required to be secured at all times by collateral in an amount at least equal to the market value of securities loaned. Daily market fluctuations could cause the value of loaned securities to be more or less than the value of the collateral received. When this occurs, the collateral is adjusted and settled on the next business day. The fund further mitigates its counterparty risk by entering into securities lending transactions only with a diverse group of prequalified counterparties, monitoring their financial strength, and entering into master securities lending agreements with its counterparties. The master securities lending agreements provide that, in the event of a counterparty&#8217;s default (including bankruptcy), the fund may terminate any loans with that borrower, determine the net amount owed, and sell or retain the collateral up to the net amount owed to the fund; however, such actions may be subject to legal proceedings. While collateral mitigates counterparty risk, in the absence of a default the fund may experience delays and costs in recovering the securities loaned. The fund invests cash collateral received in Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund, and records a liability in the Statement of Net Assets for the return of the collateral, during the period the securities are on loan. Securities lending income represents fees charged to borrowers plus income earned on invested cash collateral, less expenses associated with the loan.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>6. Credit Facility: The fund and certain other funds managed by The Vanguard Group (&#8220;Vanguard&#8221;) participate in a $3 billion committed credit facility provided by a syndicate of lenders pursuant to a credit agreement that may be renewed annually; each fund is individually liable for its borrowings, if any, under the credit facility. Borrowings may be utilized for temporary and emergency purposes, and are subject to the fund&#8217;s regulatory and contractual borrowing restrictions. The participating funds are charged administrative fees and an annual commitment fee of 0.06% of the undrawn amount of the facility; these fees are allocated to the funds based on a method approved by the fund&#8217;s board of trustees and included in Management and Administrative expenses on the fund&#8217;s Statement of Operations. Any borrowings under this facility bear interest at a rate equal to the higher of the federal funds rate or LIBOR reference rate plus an agreed-upon spread.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The fund had no borrowings outstanding at December 31, 2015, or at any time during the period then ended.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>7</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>. Other: Dividend income is recorded on the ex-dividend date. Interest income includes income distributions received from Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund and is accrued daily. Premiums and discounts on debt securities purchased are amortized and accreted, respectively, to interest income over the lives of the respective securities. Security transactions are accounted for on the date securities are bought or sold. Costs used to determine realized gains (losses) on the sale of investment securities are those of the specific securities sold.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Unrealized appreciation (depreciation) on open futures contracts is required to be treated as realized gain (loss) for tax purposes.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>E. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Distributions are determined on a tax basis and may differ from net investment income and realized capital gains for financial reporting purposes. Differences may be permanent or temporary. Permanent differences are reclassified among capital accounts in the financial statements to reflect their tax character. Temporary differences arise when certain items of income, expense, gain, or loss are recognized in different periods for financial statement and tax purposes. These differences will reverse at some time in the future. Differences in classification may also result from the treatment of short-term gains as ordinary income for tax purposes.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>During the year ended December 31, 2015, the fund realized $1,9</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>47</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>,</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>8</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>55,000 of net capital gains resulting from in-kind redemptions&#8212;in which shareholders exchanged fund shares for securities held by the fund rather than for cash. Because such gains are not taxable to the fund, and are not distributed to shareholders, they have been reclassified from accumulated net realized losses to paid-in capital.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>For tax purposes, at December 31, 2015, the fund had $16,</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>4</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>12,000 of ordinary income available for distribution. <P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Value Index Fund</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=3 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Notes to Financial Statements</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Vanguard Value Index Fund is registered under the Investment Company Act of 19</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>4</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>0 as an open-end investment company, or mutual fund. The fund offers four classes of shares: Investor Shares, ETF Shares, Admiral Shares, and Institutional Shares. Investor Shares are available to any investor who meets the fund&#8217;s minimum purchase requirements. ETF Shares are listed for trading on NYSE Arca; they can be purchased and sold through a broker. Admiral Shares and Institutional Shares are designed for investors who meet certain administrative, service, and account-size criteria. Prior to October 2</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>4</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>, 201</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>4</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>, the fund offered Signal Shares. Effective at the close of business on October 2</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>4</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>, 201</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>4</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>, the Signal Shares were converted to Admiral Shares.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>A. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The following significant accounting policies conform to generally accepted accounting principles for U.S. investment companies. The fund consistently follows such policies in preparing its financial statements.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>1. Security Valuation: Securities are valued as of the close of trading on the New York Stock Exchange (generally </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>4 </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>p.m., Eastern time) on the valuation date. Equity securities are valued at the latest quoted sales prices or official closing prices taken from the primary market in which each security trades; such securities not traded on the valuation date are valued at the mean of the latest quoted bid and asked prices. Securities for which market quotations are not readily available, or whose values have been materially affected by events occurring before the fund&#8217;s pricing time but after the close of the securities&#8217; primary markets, are valued by methods deemed by the board of trustees to represent fair value. Investments in Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund are valued at that fund&#8217;s net asset value. Temporary cash investments acquired over 60 days to maturity are valued using the latest bid prices or using valuations based on a matrix system (which considers such factors as security prices, yields, maturities, and ratings), both as furnished by independent pricing services. Other temporary cash investments are valued at amortized cost, which approximates market value.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>2. Futures Contracts: The fund uses index futures contracts to a limited extent, with the objectives of maintaining full exposure to the stock market, enhancing returns, maintaining liquidity, and minimizing transaction costs. The fund may purchase futures contracts to immediately invest incoming cash in the market, or sell futures in response to cash outflows, thereby simulating a fully invested position in the underlying index while maintaining a cash balance for liquidity. The fund may seek to enhance returns by using futures contracts instead of the underlying securities when futures are believed to be priced more attractively than the underlying securities. The primary risks associated with the use of futures contracts are imperfect correlation between changes in market values of stocks held by the fund and the prices of futures contracts, and the possibility of an illiquid market. Counterparty risk involving futures is mitigated because a regulated clearinghouse is the counterparty instead of the clearing broker. To further mitigate counterparty risk, the fund trades futures contracts on an exchange, monitors the financial strength of its clearing brokers and clearinghouse, and has entered into clearing agreements with its clearing brokers. The clearinghouse imposes initial margin requirements to secure the fund&#8217;s performance and requires daily settlement of variation margin representing changes in the market value of each contract.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Futures contracts are valued at their quoted daily settlement prices. The aggregate settlement values of the contracts are not recorded in the Statement of Net Assets. Fluctuations in the value of the contracts are recorded in the Statement of Net Assets as an asset (liability) and in the Statement of Operations as unrealized appreciation (depreciation) until the contracts are closed, when they are recorded as realized futures gains (losses).</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Value Index Fund</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>During the year ended December 31, 2015, the fund&#8217;s average investments in long and short futures contracts represented less than 1% and 0% of net assets, respectively, based on the average of aggregate settlement values at each quarter-end during the period.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>3. Federal Income Taxes: The fund intends to continue to qualify as a regulated investment company and distribute all of its taxable income. Management has analyzed the fund&#8217;s tax positions taken for all open federal income tax years (December 31, 2012&#8211;2015), and has concluded that no provision for federal income tax is required in the fund&#8217;s financial statements.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>4</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>. Distributions: Distributions to shareholders are recorded on the ex-dividend date.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>5. Securities Lending: To earn additional income, the fund lends its securities to qualified institutional borrowers. Security loans are subject to termination by the fund at any time and are required to be secured at all times by collateral in an amount at least equal to the market value of securities loaned. Daily market fluctuations could cause the value of loaned securities to be more or less than the value of the collateral received. When this occurs, the collateral is adjusted and settled on the next business day. The fund further mitigates its counterparty risk by entering into securities lending transactions only with a diverse group of prequalified counterparties, monitoring their financial strength, and entering into master securities lending agreements with its counterparties. The master securities lending agreements provide that, in the event of a counterparty&#8217;s default (including bankruptcy), the fund may terminate any loans with that borrower, determine the net amount owed, and sell or retain the collateral up to the net amount owed to the fund; however, such actions may be subject to legal proceedings. While collateral mitigates counterparty risk, in the absence of a default the fund may experience delays and costs in recovering the securities loaned. The fund invests cash collateral received in Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund, and records a liability in the Statement of Net Assets for the return of the collateral, during the period the securities are on loan. Securities lending income represents fees charged to borrowers plus income earned on invested cash collateral, less expenses associated with the loan.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>6. Credit Facility: The fund and certain other funds managed by The Vanguard Group (&#8220;Vanguard&#8221;) participate in a $3 billion committed credit facility provided by a syndicate of lenders pursuant to a credit agreement that may be renewed annually; each fund is individually liable for its borrowings, if any, under the credit facility. Borrowings may be utilized for temporary and emergency purposes, and are subject to the fund&#8217;s regulatory and contractual borrowing restrictions. The participating funds are charged administrative fees and an annual commitment fee of 0.06% of the undrawn amount of the facility; these fees are allocated to the funds based on a method approved by the fund&#8217;s board of trustees and included in Management and Administrative expenses on the fund&#8217;s Statement of Operations. Any borrowings under this facility bear interest at a rate equal to the higher of the federal funds rate or LIBOR reference rate plus an agreed-upon spread.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The fund had no borrowings outstanding at December 31, 2015, or at any time during the period then ended.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>7</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>. Other: Dividend income is recorded on the ex-dividend date. Interest income includes income distributions received from Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund and is accrued daily. Premiums and discounts on debt securities purchased are amortized and accreted, respectively, to interest income over the lives of the respective securities. Security transactions are accounted for on the date securities are bought or sold. Costs used to determine realized gains (losses) on the sale of investment securities are those of the specific securities sold.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Unrealized appreciation (depreciation) on open futures contracts is required to be treated as realized gain (loss) for tax purposes.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>E. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Distributions are determined on a tax basis and may differ from net investment income and realized capital gains for financial reporting purposes. Differences may be permanent or temporary. Permanent differences are reclassified among capital accounts in the financial statements to reflect their tax character. Temporary differences arise when certain items of income, expense, gain, or loss are recognized in different periods for financial statement and tax purposes. These differences will reverse at some time in the future. Differences in classification may also result from the treatment of short-term gains as ordinary income for tax purposes.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>During the year ended December 31, 2015, the fund realized $1,2</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>4</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>9,696,000 of net capital gains resulting from in-kind redemptions&#8212;in which shareholders exchanged fund shares for securities held by the fund rather than for cash. Because such gains are not taxable to the fund, and are not distributed to shareholders, they have been reclassified from accumulated net realized losses to paid-in capital.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>For tax purposes, at December 31, 2015, the fund had $9,6</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>88</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>,000 of ordinary income available for distribution. At December 31, 2015, the fund had available capital losses totaling $605,</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>4</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>15,000 to offset future net capital gains. <P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Large-Cap Index Fund</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=3 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Notes to Financial Statements</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Vanguard Large-Cap Index Fund is registered under the Investment Company Act of 19</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>4</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>0 as an open-end investment company, or mutual fund. The fund offers four classes of shares: Investor Shares, ETF Shares, Admiral Shares, and Institutional Shares. Investor Shares are available to any investor who meets the fund&#8217;s minimum purchase requirements. ETF Shares are listed for trading on NYSE Arca; they can be purchased and sold through a broker. Admiral Shares and Institutional Shares are designed for investors who meet certain administrative, service, and account-size criteria. Prior to October 2</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>4</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>, 201</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>4</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>, the fund offered Signal Shares. Effective at the close of business on October 2</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>4</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>, 201</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>4</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>, the Signal Shares were converted to Admiral Shares.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>A. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The following significant accounting policies conform to generally accepted accounting principles for U.S. investment companies. The fund consistently follows such policies in preparing its financial statements.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>1. Security Valuation: Securities are valued as of the close of trading on the New York Stock Exchange (generally </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>4 </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>p.m., Eastern time) on the valuation date. Equity securities are valued at the latest quoted sales prices or official closing prices taken from the primary market in which each security trades; such securities not traded on the valuation date are valued at the mean of the latest quoted bid and asked prices. Securities for which market quotations are not readily available, or whose values have been materially affected by events occurring before the fund&#8217;s pricing time but after the close of the securities&#8217; primary markets, are valued by methods deemed by the board of trustees to represent fair value. Investments in Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund are valued at that fund&#8217;s net asset value. Temporary cash investments acquired over 60 days to maturity are valued using the latest bid prices or using valuations based on a matrix system (which considers such factors as security prices, yields, maturities, and ratings), both as furnished by independent pricing services. Other temporary cash investments are valued at amortized cost, which approximates market value.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>2. Futures Contracts: The fund uses index futures contracts to a limited extent, with the objectives of maintaining full exposure to the stock market, enhancing returns, maintaining liquidity, and minimizing transaction costs. The fund may purchase futures contracts to immediately invest incoming cash in the market, or sell futures in response to cash outflows, thereby simulating a fully invested position in the underlying index while maintaining a cash balance for liquidity. The fund may seek to enhance returns by using futures contracts instead of the underlying securities when futures are believed to be priced more attractively than the underlying securities. The primary risks associated with the use of futures contracts are imperfect correlation between changes in market values of stocks held by the fund and the prices of futures contracts, and the possibility of an illiquid market. Counterparty risk involving futures is mitigated because a regulated clearinghouse is the counterparty instead of the clearing broker. To further mitigate counterparty risk, the fund trades futures contracts on an exchange, monitors the financial strength of its clearing brokers and clearinghouse, and has entered into clearing agreements with its clearing brokers. The clearinghouse imposes initial margin requirements to secure the fund&#8217;s performance and requires daily settlement of variation margin representing changes in the market value of each contract.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Futures contracts are valued at their quoted daily settlement prices. The aggregate settlement values of the contracts are not recorded in the Statement of Net Assets. Fluctuations in the value of the contracts are recorded in the Statement of Net Assets as an asset (liability) and in the Statement of Operations as unrealized appreciation (depreciation) until the contracts are closed, when they are recorded as realized futures gains (losses).</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>72</FONT></P></DIV>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Large-Cap Index Fund</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>During the year ended December 31, 2015, the fund&#8217;s average investments in long and short futures contracts represented less than 1% and 0% of net assets, respectively, based on the average of aggregate settlement values at each quarter-end during the period.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>3. Federal Income Taxes: The fund intends to continue to qualify as a regulated investment company and distribute all of its taxable income. Management has analyzed the fund&#8217;s tax positions taken for all open federal income tax years (December 31, 2012&#8211;2015), and has concluded that no provision for federal income tax is required in the fund&#8217;s financial statements.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>4</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>. Distributions: Distributions to shareholders are recorded on the ex-dividend date.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>5. Securities Lending: To earn additional income, the fund lends its securities to qualified institutional borrowers. Security loans are subject to termination by the fund at any time and are required to be secured at all times by collateral in an amount at least equal to the market value of securities loaned. Daily market fluctuations could cause the value of loaned securities to be more or less than the value of the collateral received. When this occurs, the collateral is adjusted and settled on the next business day. The fund further mitigates its counterparty risk by entering into securities lending transactions only with a diverse group of prequalified counterparties, monitoring their financial strength, and entering into master securities lending agreements with its counterparties. The master securities lending agreements provide that, in the event of a counterparty&#8217;s default (including bankruptcy), the fund may terminate any loans with that borrower, determine the net amount owed, and sell or retain the collateral up to the net amount owed to the fund; however, such actions may be subject to legal proceedings. While collateral mitigates counterparty risk, in the absence of a default the fund may experience delays and costs in recovering the securities loaned. The fund invests cash collateral received in Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund, and records a liability in the Statement of Net Assets for the return of the collateral, during the period the securities are on loan. Securities lending income represents fees charged to borrowers plus income earned on invested cash collateral, less expenses associated with the loan.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>6. Credit Facility: The fund and certain other funds managed by The Vanguard Group (&#8220;Vanguard&#8221;) participate in a $3 billion committed credit facility provided by a syndicate of lenders pursuant to a credit agreement that may be renewed annually; each fund is individually liable for its borrowings, if any, under the credit facility. Borrowings may be utilized for temporary and emergency purposes, and are subject to the fund&#8217;s regulatory and contractual borrowing restrictions. The participating funds are charged administrative fees and an annual commitment fee of 0.06% of the undrawn amount of the facility; these fees are allocated to the funds based on a method approved by the fund&#8217;s board of trustees and included in Management and Administrative expenses on the fund&#8217;s Statement of Operations. Any borrowings under this facility bear interest at a rate equal to the higher of the federal funds rate or LIBOR reference rate plus an agreed-upon spread.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The fund had no borrowings outstanding at December 31, 2015, or at any time during the period then ended.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>7</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>. Other: Dividend income is recorded on the ex-dividend date. Interest income includes income distributions received from Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund and is accrued daily. Premiums and discounts on debt securities purchased are amortized and accreted, respectively, to interest income over the lives of the respective securities. Security transactions are accounted for on the date securities are bought or sold. Costs used to determine realized gains (losses) on the sale of investment securities are those of the specific securities sold.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>E. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Distributions are determined on a tax basis and may differ from net investment income and realized capital gains for financial reporting purposes. <P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=3 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Your Fund&#8217;s After-Tax Returns</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>This table presents returns for your fund both before and after taxes. The after-tax returns are shown in two ways: (1) assuming that an investor owned the fund during the entire period and paid taxes on the fund&#8217;s distributions, and (2) assuming that an investor paid taxes on the fund&#8217;s distributions </FONT><I><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-LightObl,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>and </FONT></I><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>sold all shares at the end of each period.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Calculations are based on the highest individual federal income tax and capital gains tax rates in effect at the times of the distributions and the hypothetical sales. State and local taxes were not considered. After-tax returns reflect any qualified dividend income. (In the example, returns after the sale of fund shares may be higher than those assuming no sale. This occurs when the sale would have produced a capital loss. The calculation assumes that the investor received a tax deduction for the loss.)</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The table shows returns for Investor Shares only; returns for other share classes will differ. Also note that if you own the fund in a tax-deferred account, such as an individual retirement account or a 401(k) plan, this information does not apply to you. Such accounts are not subject to current taxes.</FONT></P>

<DIV style=" PADDING-LEFT: 0%; PADDING-RIGHT: 0%">

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=3 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>About Your Fund&#8217;s Expenses</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>As a shareholder of the fund, you incur ongoing costs, which include costs for portfolio management, administrative services, and shareholder reports (like this one), among others. Operating expenses, which are deducted from a fund&#8217;s gross income, directly reduce the investment return of the fund.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>A fund&#8217;s expenses are expressed as a percentage of its average net assets. This figure is known as the expense ratio. The following examples are intended to help you understand the ongoing costs (in dollars) of investing in your fund and to compare these costs with those of other mutual funds. The examples are based on an investment of $1,000 made at the beginning of the period shown and held for the entire period.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The accompanying table illustrates your fund&#8217;s costs in two ways:</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>&#8226; </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Based on actual fund return. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>This section helps you to estimate the actual expenses that you paid over the period. The &#8221;Ending Account Value&#8220; shown is derived from the fund&#8216;s actual return, and the third column shows the dollar amount that would have been paid by an investor who started with $1,000 in the fund. You may use the information here, together with the amount you invested, to estimate the expenses that you paid over the period.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>To do so, simply divide your account value by $1,000 (for example, an $8,600 account value divided by $1,000 = 8.6), then multiply the result by the number given for your fund under the heading &#8221;Expenses Paid During Period.&#8220;</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>&#8226; </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Based on hypothetical 5% yearly return. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>This section is intended to help you compare your fund&#8216;s costs with those of other mutual funds. It assumes that the fund had a yearly return of 5% before expenses, but that the expense ratio is unchanged. In this case&#8212;because the return used is not the fund&#8217;s actual return&#8212;the results do not apply to your investment. The example is useful in making comparisons because the Securities and Exchange Commission requires all mutual funds to calculate expenses based on a 5% return. You can assess your fund&#8217;s costs by comparing this hypothetical example with the hypothetical examples that appear in shareholder reports of other funds.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Univers-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Note that the expenses shown in the table are meant to highlight and help you compare </FONT><I><FONT size=1 face=Univers-LightOblique,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>ongoing </FONT></I><FONT size=1 face=Univers-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>costs only and do not reflect transaction costs incurred by the fund for buying and selling securities. Further, the expenses do not include any purchase, redemption, or account service fees described in the fund prospectus. If such fees were applied to your account, your costs would be higher. Your fund does not carry a &#8220;sales load.&#8221;</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The calculations assume no shares were bought or sold during the period. Your actual costs may have been higher or lower, depending on the amount of your investment and the timing of any purchases or redemptions.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>You can find more information about the fund&#8217;s expenses, including annual expense ratios, in the Financial Statements section of this report. For additional information on operating expenses and other shareholder costs, please refer to your fund&#8217;s current prospectus.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-LightCn,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The calculations are based on expenses incurred in the most recent six-month period. The funds&#8217; annualized six-month expense ratios for that period are: for the Growth Index Fund, 0.23% for Investor Shares, 0.09% for ETF Shares, 0.09% for Admiral Shares, and 0.07% for Institutional Shares; for the Value Index Fund, 0.23% for Investor Shares, 0.09% for ETF Shares, 0.09% for Admiral Shares, and 0.08% for Institutional Shares; and for the Large-Cap Index Fund, 0.18% for Investor Shares, 0.09% for ETF Shares, 0.09% for Admiral Shares, and 0.08% for Institutional Shares. The dollar amounts shown as &#8220;Expenses Paid&#8221; are equal to the annualized expense ratio multiplied by the average account value over the period, multiplied by the number of days in the most recent six-month period, then divided by the number of days in the most recent 12-month period (184/365).</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>82</FONT></P></DIV>

<DIV style="PAGE-BREAK-BEFORE: always">&nbsp;</DIV>

<!--$$/page=--><A name="page_322"></A><BR>

<DIV style=" PADDING-LEFT: 0%; PADDING-RIGHT: 0%">

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=3 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Glossary</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>30-Day SEC Yield. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>A fund&#8217;s 30-day SEC yield is derived using a formula specified by the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission. Under the formula, data related to the fund&#8217;s security holdings in the previous 30 days are used to calculate the fund&#8217;s hypothetical net income for that period, which is then annualized and divided by the fund&#8217;s estimated average net assets over the calculation period. For the purposes of this calculation, a security&#8217;s income is based on its current market yield to maturity (for bonds), its actual income (for asset-backed securities), or its projected dividend yield (for stocks). Because the SEC yield represents hypothetical annualized income, it will differ&#8212;at times significantly&#8212;from the fund&#8217;s actual experience. As a result, the fund&#8217;s income distributions may be higher or lower than implied by the SEC yield.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Beta. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>A measure of the magnitude of a fund&#8217;s past share-price fluctuations in relation to the ups and downs of a given market index. The index is assigned a beta of 1.00. Compared with a given index, a fund with a beta of 1.20 typically would have seen its share price rise or fall by 12% when the index rose or fell by 10%. For this report, beta is based on returns over the past 36 months for both the fund and the index. Note that a fund&#8217;s beta should be reviewed in conjunction with its R-squared (see definition). The lower the R-squared, the less correlation there is between the fund and the index, and the less reliable beta is as an indicator of volatility.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Dividend Yield. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Dividend income earned by stocks, expressed as a percentage of the aggregate market value (or of net asset value, for a fund). The yield is determined by dividing the amount of the annual dividends by the aggregate value (or net asset value) at the end of the period. For a fund, the dividend yield is based solely on stock holdings and does not include any income produced by other investments.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Earnings Growth Rate. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The average annual rate of growth in earnings over the past five years for the stocks now in a fund.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Equity Exposure. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>A measure that reflects a fund&#8217;s investments in stocks and stock futures. Any holdings in short-term reserves are excluded.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Expense Ratio. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>A fund&#8217;s total annual operating expenses expressed as a percentage of the fund&#8217;s average net assets. The expense ratio includes management and administrative expenses, but does not include the transaction costs of buying and selling portfolio securities.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Foreign Holdings. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The percentage of a fund represented by securities or depositary receipts of companies based outside the United States.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Inception Date. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The date on which the assets of a fund (or one of its share classes) are first invested in accordance with the fund&#8217;s investment objective. For funds with a subscription period, the inception date is the day after that period ends. Investment performance is measured from the inception date.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Median Market Cap. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>An indicator of the size of companies in which a fund invests; the midpoint of market capitalization (market price x shares outstanding) of a fund&#8217;s stocks, weighted by the proportion of the fund&#8217;s assets invested in each stock. Stocks representing half of the fund&#8217;s assets have market capitalizations above the median, and the rest are below it.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Price/Book Ratio. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The share price of a stock divided by its net worth, or book value, per share. For a fund, the weighted average price/book ratio of the stocks it holds.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>83</FONT></P></DIV>

<DIV style="PAGE-BREAK-BEFORE: always">&nbsp;</DIV>

<!--$$/page=--><A name="page_323"></A><BR>

<DIV style=" PADDING-LEFT: 0%; PADDING-RIGHT: 0%">

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Price/Earnings Ratio. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The ratio of a stock&#8217;s current price to its per-share earnings over the past year. For a fund, the weighted average P/E of the stocks it holds. P/E is an indicator of market expectations about corporate prospects; the higher the P/E, the greater the expectations for a company&#8217;s future growth.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>R-Squared. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>A measure of how much of a fund&#8217;s past returns can be explained by the returns from the market in general, as measured by a given index. If a fund&#8217;s total returns were precisely synchronized with an index&#8217;s returns, its R-squared would be 1.00. If the fund&#8217;s returns bore no relationship to the index&#8217;s returns, its R-squared would be 0. For this report, R-squared is based on returns over the past 36 months for both the fund and the index.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Return on Equity. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The annual average rate of return generated by a company during the past five years for each dollar of shareholder&#8217;s equity (net income divided by shareholder&#8217;s equity). For a fund, the weighted average return on equity for the companies whose stocks it holds.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Short-Term Reserves. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The percentage of a fund invested in highly liquid, short-term securities that can be readily converted to cash.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Turnover Rate. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>An indication of the fund&#8217;s trading activity. Funds with high turnover rates incur higher transaction costs and may be more likely to distribute capital gains (which may be taxable to investors). The turnover rate excludes in-kind transactions, which have minimal impact on costs.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Benchmark Information</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Spliced Growth Index: </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>S&amp;P 500 Growth Index (formerly known as the S&amp;P 500/Barra Growth Index) through May 16, 2003;&nbsp;MSCI US Prime Market Growth Index through April 16, 2013; CRSP US Large Cap Growth Index thereafter.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Spliced Large Cap Index: </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>MSCI US Prime Market 750 Index through January 30, 2013; CRSP US Large Cap Index thereafter.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Spliced Value Index: </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>S&amp;P 500 Value Index (formerly known as the S&amp;P 500/Barra Value Index) through May 16, 2003; MSCI US Prime Market Value Index through April 16, 2013; CRSP US Large Cap Value Index thereafter.</FONT></P>

<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=2 face="Univers,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Vanguard&#146;s Principles for Investing Success</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=2 face="Univers-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">We want to give you the best chance of investment success. These principles, grounded in Vanguard&#146;s research and experience, can put you on the right path.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=2 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Goals. </FONT><FONT size=2 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Create clear, appropriate investment goals.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=2 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Balance. </FONT><FONT size=2 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Develop a suitable asset allocation using broadly diversified funds. </FONT><FONT size=2 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Cost. </FONT><FONT size=2 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Minimize cost.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=2 face="UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Discipline. </FONT><FONT size=2 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Maintain perspective and long-term discipline.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=2 face="Univers-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">A single theme unites these principles: Focus on the things you can control.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=2 face="Univers-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">We believe there is no wiser course for any investor.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>1</FONT></P></DIV>

<DIV style=" PADDING-LEFT: 0%; PADDING-RIGHT: 0%">
<IMG border=0 src="totalstockmarketindexfunx4x1.jpg"> <BR>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=3 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Chairman&#8217;s Letter</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Dear Shareholder,</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Buffeted by various global economic and market challenges, U.S. stocks traced a roundabout route in 2015 before finishing slightly ahead of where they started. Over the 12-month period ended December 31, 2015, Vanguard Total Stock Market Index Fund&#8217;s Investor Shares returned 0.29%. The fund closely tracked the performance of its benchmark, the CRSP US Total Market Index, and surpassed the average return of its multi-cap core fund peers by about 2 percentage points.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Growth stocks outpaced their value counterparts, and large-capitalization stocks exceeded mid-caps and small-caps. Six of the market&#8217;s ten industry sectors posted positive results. Consumer and health care stocks were the top performers, while oil and gas and basic materials stocks noticeably lagged.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>A broad stock market index fund can be a tax-efficient investment. If you hold the fund in a taxable account, you may wish to review the after-tax returns that appear later in this report.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Despite troubles, U.S. stocks </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>eked out a seventh year of gains</FONT><BR><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>U.S. stocks returned 0.48% for the </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>12 months. Although the broad market </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>recorded its worst performance since </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>2008, it still posted gains for the seventh </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>straight calendar year when dividends </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>are factored into returns.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>2</FONT></P></DIV>

<DIV style="PAGE-BREAK-BEFORE: always">&nbsp;</DIV>

<!--$$/page=--><A name="page_334"></A><BR>

<DIV style=" PADDING-LEFT: 0%; PADDING-RIGHT: 0%">

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Stocks rose modestly over the first half of the year but slid in August and September as concerns mounted that China&#8217;s economic slowdown would spread globally. Falling oil and commodity prices also affected economies and markets across the world for better or worse. Central banks in Europe and Asia bolstered their stimulus efforts against weak growth and low inflation. And in December, the Federal Reserve ended months of uncertainty when it raised the target for short-term interest rates to 0.25%&#8211;0.5%.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>International stocks returned about &#8211;5%, restrained by the U.S. dollar&#8217;s strength against many foreign currencies. Emerging markets fared the worst.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>U.S. bonds ended the year with a slender advance</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The broad U.S. taxable bond market gained 0.55% over the 12 months; income accounted for the modestly positive result. The yield of the 10-year Treasury note ended December at 2.30%, up from 2.19% a year earlier. (Bond prices and yields move in opposite directions.)</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Investors focused on the Fed&#8217;s stance on short-term interest rates and alternately embraced or avoided safe-haven assets, depending on the stock market&#8217;s strength.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>International bond markets (as measured by the Barclays Global Aggregate Index ex USD) returned &#8211;6.02%, reduced by the</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>dollar&#8217;s strength against many foreign currencies. Without this currency effect, returns were modestly positive.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Although the Fed raised its target for short-term interest rates in mid-December, returns for money market funds and savings accounts remained limited by the 0%&#8211;0.25% levels in place for much of the past seven years.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Oil and gas stocks&#8217; fall continued; consumer sectors were bright spots</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Vanguard Total Stock Market Index Fund offers investors exposure to every segment of the U.S. equity market. Stocks of all sizes, styles, and sectors are represented. For this period, the fund&#8217;s overall performance was helped by its heavy exposure to large-cap stocks.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The retreat of oil and gas stocks, which returned about &#8211;22% over the period, had the largest impact on the fund&#8217;s overall results. Oil prices&#8217; lengthy and sharp slide punished the sector, in part because of high production levels from some leading oil-producing countries and the concerns about China, the world&#8217;s largest oil importer. Natural gas prices also dropped, though not as dramatically. Some integrated oil and gas firms held up better than others, but most companies engaged in production and exploration and services and distribution suffered.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The basic materials sector, which returned &#8211;12%, was another of the broad market&#8217;s weakest as commodity prices fell along with those of oil. Metals and mining firms, which dominate the sector, posted the</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The investment environment wasn&#8217;t all grim. The U.S. economy mostly grew, propped up by shoppers&#8217; overall confidence and willingness to spend. Among the market&#8217;s strongest sectors were consumer services and consumer goods. In consumer services, the internet retail area was especially productive; several home improvement retailers also excelled. In consumer goods, notable showings came from toy, tobacco, and beverage companies.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Health care stocks climbed nearly 7%, results that were a fraction better than those of consumer services and the best of the ten sectors. Merger-and-acquisition activity, vibrant drug pipelines, and favorable long-term demographic and economic trends lifted the sector, but there were stumbles related to controversy over high drug prices and lofty valuations of biotechnology stocks.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Technology returned almost 4%. As with health care, results paled compared with some robust recent periods but were still positive. Gains from internet and software firms were partially offset by poorer performance from computer hardware and semiconductor companies.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Tight tracking is evident over the previous decade</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Over the last ten years, the Total Stock Market Index Fund&#8217;s Investor Shares have produced an average annual return of 7.39%, in line with the benchmark and </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>more than 1 percentage point higher than peer funds, many of which are actively managed.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>This group of professionals uses well-honed portfolio construction and trading methodologies that have allowed Vanguard to provide effective index-tracking regardless of the market&#8217;s volatility or direction.</FONT></P>
