<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The fund has also benefited from its low costs, which help close the gap between the index&#8217;s results and yours.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>To reach your long-term goals, be realistic and try to save more</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Although there have been times when it felt as if stocks and bonds were riding a roller coaster, the markets have generally risen in recent years. The broad global stock market in particular has posted some impressive gains since its turnaround began in 2009.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>But 2015 served as a reminder that markets aren&#8217;t always favorable. The U.S. stock and bond markets were barely positive, and international stocks and unhedged bonds finished in the red.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>In Vanguard&#8217;s recently updated long-term look at the economy and markets, our global economists explain why they expect economic growth to remain &#8220;frustratingly fragile&#8221; and why their outlook for stock and bond markets is the most guarded since 2006. (For more details, see the box on page 6 and </FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-LightObl,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Vanguard&#8217;s Economic and Investment Outlook</FONT><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>, available at vanguard. com/research.)</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Given these muted expectations, what&#8217;s the best course of action? I&#8217;ve often encouraged shareholders to focus on the things they can control. That advice holds true today.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Consider saving more than you think you may need. That&#8217;s one way you can prepare for the volatility that may lie ahead,</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Cn,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>IMPORTANT: The projections or other information generated by the Vanguard Capital Markets Model (VCMM) regarding the likelihood of various investment outcomes are hypothetical in nature, do not reflect actual investment results, and are not guarantees of future results. VCMM results will vary with each use and over time.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-LightCn,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The VCMM projections are based on a statistical analysis of historical data. Future returns may behave differently from the historical patterns captured in the VCMM. More important, the VCMM may be underestimating extreme negative scenarios unobserved in the historical period on which the model estimation is based.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-LightCn,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The VCMM is a proprietary financial simulation tool developed and maintained by Vanguard&#8217;s primary investment research and advice teams. The model forecasts distributions of future returns for a wide array of broad asset classes. Those asset classes include U.S. and international equity markets, several maturities of the U.S. Treasury and corporate fixed income markets, international fixed income markets, U.S. money markets, commodities, and certain alternative investment strategies. The theoretical and empirical foundation for the VCMM is that the returns of various asset classes reflect the compensation investors require for bearing different types of systematic risk (beta). At the core of the model are estimates of the dynamic statistical relationship between risk factors and asset returns, obtained from statistical analysis based on available monthly financial and economic data from as early as 1960. Using a system of estimated equations, the model then applies a Monte Carlo simulation method to project the estimated interrelationships among risk factors and asset classes as well as uncertainty and randomness over time. The model generates a large set of simulated outcomes for each asset class over several time horizons. Forecasts are obtained by computing measures of central tendency in these simulations. Results produced by the tool will vary with each use and over time.</FONT></P>

<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=2 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">particularly as markets adjust to changes in policies from the Fed and other central banks.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=2 face="UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">And, as always, investors would be well-served to follow Vanguard&#146;s principles for investing success:</FONT></P>

<DIV style=" PADDING-LEFT: 0%; PADDING-RIGHT: 0%">

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Total Stock Market Index Fund</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=3 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Notes to Financial Statements</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Vanguard Total Stock Market Index Fund is registered under the Investment Company Act of 19</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>4</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>0 as an open-end investment company, or mutual fund. The fund offers five classes of shares: Investor Shares, ETF Shares, Admiral Shares, Institutional Shares, and Institutional Plus Shares. Investor Shares are available to any investor who meets the fund&#8217;s minimum purchase requirements. ETF Shares are listed for trading on NYSE Arca; they can be purchased and sold through a broker. Admiral Shares, Institutional Shares, and Institutional Plus Shares are designed for investors who meet certain administrative, service, and account-size criteria. Prior to October 2</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>4</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>, 201</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>4</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>, the fund offered Signal Shares. Effective October 2</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>4</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>, 201</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>4</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>, the Signal Shares were converted to Admiral Shares.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>A. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The following significant accounting policies conform to generally accepted accounting principles for U.S. investment companies. The fund consistently follows such policies in preparing its financial statements.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>1. Security Valuation: Securities are valued as of the close of trading on the New York Stock Exchange (generally </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>4 </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>p.m., Eastern time) on the valuation date. Equity securities are valued at the latest quoted sales prices or official closing prices taken from the primary market in which each security trades; such securities not traded on the valuation date are valued at the mean of the latest quoted bid and asked prices. Securities for which market quotations are not readily available, or whose values have been materially affected by events occurring before the fund&#8217;s pricing time but after the close of the securities&#8217; primary markets, are valued by methods deemed by the board of trustees to represent fair value. Investments in Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund are valued at that fund&#8217;s net asset value. Temporary cash investments acquired over 60 days to maturity are valued using the latest bid prices or using valuations based on a matrix system (which considers such factors as security prices, yields, maturities, and ratings), both as furnished by independent pricing services. Other temporary cash investments are valued at amortized cost, which approximates market value.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>2. Futures Contracts: The fund uses index futures contracts to a limited extent, with the objectives of maintaining full exposure to the stock market, enhancing returns, maintaining liquidity, and minimizing transaction costs. The fund may purchase futures contracts to immediately invest incoming cash in the market, or sell futures in response to cash outflows, thereby simulating a fully invested position in the underlying index while maintaining a cash balance for liquidity. The fund may seek to enhance returns by using futures contracts instead of the underlying securities when futures are believed to be priced more attractively than the underlying securities. The primary risks associated with the use of futures contracts are imperfect correlation between changes in market values of stocks held by the fund and the prices of futures contracts, and the possibility of an illiquid market. Counterparty risk involving futures is mitigated because a regulated clearinghouse is the counterparty instead of the clearing broker. To further mitigate counterparty risk, the fund trades futures contracts on an exchange, monitors the financial strength of its clearing brokers and clearinghouse, and has entered into clearing agreements with its clearing brokers. The clearinghouse imposes initial margin requirements to secure the fund&#8217;s performance and requires daily settlement of variation margin representing changes in the market value of each contract.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Futures contracts are valued at their quoted daily settlement prices. The aggregate settlement values of the contracts are not recorded in the Statement of Net Assets. Fluctuations in the value of the contracts are recorded in the Statement of Net Assets as an asset (liability) and in the Statement of Operations as unrealized appreciation (depreciation) until the contracts are closed, when they are recorded as realized futures gains (losses).</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>24</FONT></P></DIV>

<DIV style="PAGE-BREAK-BEFORE: always">&nbsp;</DIV>

<!--$$/page=--><A name="page_356"></A><BR>

<DIV style=" PADDING-LEFT: 0%; PADDING-RIGHT: 0%">

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Total Stock Market Index Fund</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>During the year ended December 31, 2015, the fund&#8217;s average investments in long and short futures contracts represented less than 1% and 0% of net assets, respectively, based on the average of aggregate settlement values at each quarter-end during the period.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>3. Swap Contracts: The fund has entered into equity swap contracts to earn the total return on selected reference stocks in the fund&#8217;s target index. Under the terms of the swaps, the fund receives the total return on the referenced stock (i.e., receiving the increase or paying the decrease in value of the selected reference stock and receiving the equivalent of any dividends in respect of the selected referenced stock) over a specified period of time, applied to a notional amount that represents the value of a designated number of shares of the selected reference stock at the beginning of the equity swap contract. The fund also pays a floating rate that is based on short-term interest rates, applied to the notional amount. At the same time, the fund invests an amount approximating the notional amount of the swap in high-quality temporary cash investments.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The notional amounts of swap contracts are not recorded in the Statement of Net Assets. Swaps are valued daily based on market quotations received from independent pricing services or recognized dealers and the change in value is recorded in the Statement of Net Assets as an asset (liability) and in the Statement of Operations as unrealized appreciation (depreciation) until termination of the swap, at which time realized gain (loss) is recorded. A risk associated with all types of swaps is the possibility that a counterparty may default on its obligation to pay net amounts due to the fund. The fund&#8217;s maximum amount subject to counterparty risk is the unrealized appreciation on the swap contract. The fund mitigates its counterparty risk by entering into swaps only with a diverse group of prequalified counterparties, monitoring their financial strength, entering into master netting arrangements with its counterparties, and requiring its counterparties to transfer collateral as security for their performance. In the event of a counterparty&#8217;s default (including bankruptcy), the fund may terminate any swap contracts with that counterparty, determine the net amount owed by either party in accordance with its master netting arrangements, and sell or retain any collateral held up to the net amount owed to the fund under the master netting arrangements. The swap contracts contain provisions whereby a counterparty may terminate open contracts if the fund net assets decline below a certain level, triggering a payment by the fund if the fund is in a net liability position at the time of the termination. The payment amount would be reduced by any collateral the fund has pledged. Any securities pledged as collateral for open contracts are noted in the Statement of Net Assets. The value of collateral received or pledged is compared daily to the value of the swap contracts exposure with each counterparty, and any difference, if in excess of a specified minimum transfer amount, is adjusted and settled within two business days.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>During the year ended December 31, 2015, the fund&#8217;s average amounts of investments in total return swaps represented less than 1% of net assets, based on the average of notional amounts at each quarter-end during the period.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>4</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>. Federal Income Taxes: The fund intends to continue to qualify as a regulated investment company and distribute all of its taxable income. Management has analyzed the fund&#8217;s tax positions taken for all open federal income tax years (December 31, 2012&#8211;2015), and has concluded that no provision for federal income tax is required in the fund&#8217;s financial statements.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>5. Distributions: Distributions to shareholders are recorded on the ex-dividend date.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>6. Securities Lending: To earn additional income, the fund lends its securities to qualified institutional borrowers. Security loans are subject to termination by the fund at any time and are required to be secured at all times by collateral in an amount at least equal to the market value of securities loaned.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>25</FONT></P></DIV>

<DIV style="PAGE-BREAK-BEFORE: always">&nbsp;</DIV>

<!--$$/page=--><A name="page_357"></A><BR>

<DIV style=" PADDING-LEFT: 0%; PADDING-RIGHT: 0%">

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Total Stock Market Index Fund</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Daily market fluctuations could cause the value of loaned securities to be more or less than the value of the collateral received. When this occurs, the collateral is adjusted and settled on the next business day. The fund further mitigates its counterparty risk by entering into securities lending transactions only with a diverse group of prequalified counterparties, monitoring their financial strength, and entering into master securities lending agreements with its counterparties. The master securities lending agreements provide that, in the event of a counterparty&#8217;s default (including bankruptcy), the fund may terminate any loans with that borrower, determine the net amount owed, and sell or retain the collateral up to the net amount owed to the fund; however, such actions may be subject to legal proceedings. While collateral mitigates counterparty risk, in the absence of a default the fund may experience delays and costs in recovering the securities loaned. The fund invests cash collateral received in Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund, and records a liability in the Statement of Net Assets for the return of the collateral, during the period the securities are on loan. Securities lending income represents fees charged to borrowers plus income earned on invested cash collateral, less expenses associated with the loan.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>7. Credit Facility: The fund and certain other funds managed by The Vanguard Group (&#8220;Vanguard&#8221;) participate in a $3 billion committed credit facility provided by a syndicate of lenders pursuant to a credit agreement that may be renewed annually; each fund is individually liable for its borrowings, if any, under the credit facility. Borrowings may be utilized for temporary and emergency purposes, and are subject to the fund&#8217;s regulatory and contractual borrowing restrictions. The participating funds are charged administrative fees and an annual commitment fee of 0.06% of the undrawn amount of the facility; these fees are allocated to the funds based on a method approved by the fund&#8217;s board of trustees and included in Management and Administrative expenses on the fund&#8217;s Statement of Operations. Any borrowings under this facility bear interest at a rate equal to the higher of the federal funds rate or LIBOR reference rate plus an agreed-upon spread.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The fund had no borrowings outstanding at December 31, 2015, or at any time during the period then ended.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>8. Other: Dividend income is recorded on the ex-dividend date. Interest income includes income distributions received from Vanguard Market Liquidity Fund and is accrued daily. Premiums and discounts on debt securities purchased are amortized and accreted, respectively, to interest income over the lives of the respective securities. Security transactions are accounted for on the date securities are bought or sold. Costs used to determine realized gains (losses) on the sale of investment securities are those of the specific securities sold.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Each class of shares has equal rights as to assets and earnings, except that each class separately bears certain class-specific expenses related to maintenance of shareholder accounts (included in Management and Administrative expenses) and shareholder reporting. Marketing and distribution expenses are allocated to each class of shares based on a method approved by the board of trustees. Income, other non-class-specific expenses, and gains and losses on investments are allocated to each class of shares based on its relative net assets.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>B. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>In accordance with the terms of a Funds&#8217; Service Agreement (the &#8220;FSA&#8221;) between Vanguard and the fund, Vanguard furnishes to the fund investment advisory, corporate management, administrative, marketing, and distribution services at Vanguard&#8217;s cost of operations (as defined by the FSA). These costs of operations are allocated to the fund based on methods and guidelines approved by the board of trustees. Vanguard does not require reimbursement in the current period for certain costs of operations (such as deferred compensation/benefits and risk/insurance costs); the fund&#8217;s liability for these costs of operations is included in Payables to Vanguard on the Statement of Net Assets.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Total Stock Market Index Fund</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Upon the request of Vanguard, the fund may invest up to 0.</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>4</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>0% of its net assets as capital in Vanguard. The fund&#8217;s trustees and officers are also directors and employees, respectively, of Vanguard.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>C. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Various inputs may be used to determine the value of the fund&#8217;s investments. These inputs are summarized in three broad levels for financial statement purposes. The inputs or methodologies used to value securities are not necessarily an indication of the risk associated with investing in those securities.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Level 1</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>&#8212;Quoted prices in active markets for identical securities.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Level 2</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>&#8212;Other significant observable inputs (including quoted prices for similar securities, interest rates, prepayment speeds, credit risk, etc.).</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Level 3</FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>&#8212;Significant unobservable inputs (including the fund&#8217;s own assumptions used to determine the fair value of investments).</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>At December 31, 2015, the counterparty had deposited in segregated accounts securities with a value of $547,000 in connection with amounts due to the fund for open swap contracts.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>E. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Distributions are determined on a tax basis and may differ from net investment income and realized capital gains for financial reporting purposes. Differences may be permanent or temporary. Permanent differences are reclassified among capital accounts in the financial statements to reflect their tax character. Temporary differences arise when certain items of income, expense, gain, or loss are recognized in different periods for financial statement and tax purposes. These differences will reverse at some time in the future. Differences in classification may also result from the treatment of short-term gains as ordinary income for tax purposes.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Certain of the fund&#8217;s investments are in securities considered to be passive foreign investment companies, for which any unrealized appreciation and/or realized gains are required to be included in distributable net income for tax purposes. During the year ended December 31, 2015, the fund realized gains on the sale of passive foreign investment companies of $18,000, which have been included in current and prior periods&#8217; taxable income; accordingly, such gains have been reclassified from accumulated net realized losses to overdistributed net investment income. Passive foreign investment companies held at December 31, 2015, had unrealized appreciation of $8,922,000, all of which has been distributed and is reflected in the balance of overdistributed net investment income.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>During the year ended December 31, 2015, the fund realized $11,693,991,000 of net capital gains resulting from in-kind redemptions&#8212;in which shareholders exchanged fund shares for securities held by the fund rather than for cash. Because such gains are not taxable to the fund, and are not distributed to shareholders, they have been reclassified from accumulated net realized losses to paid-in capital.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Realized and unrealized gains (losses) on certain of the fund&#8217;s swap contracts are treated as ordinary income (loss) for tax purposes. Realized losses of $16,047,000 on swap contracts have been reclassified from accumulated net realized losses to overdistributed net investment income.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>For tax purposes, at December 31, 2015, the fund had $118,094,000 of ordinary income available for distribution. The fund used capital loss carryforwards of $917,767,000 to offset taxable capital gains realized during the year ended December 31, 2015. At December 31, 2015, the fund had available capital losses totaling $1,270,736,000 to offset future net capital gains. Of this amount, $1,003,435,000 is subject to expiration on December 31, 2016. Capital losses of $267,301,000 realized beginning in fiscal 2011 may be carried forward indefinitely under the Regulated Investment Company Modernization Act of 2010, but must be used before any expiring loss carryforwards.</FONT></P>

The after-tax returns are shown in two ways: (1) assuming that an investor owned the fund during the entire period and paid taxes on the fund&#8217;s distributions, and (2) assuming that an investor paid taxes on the fund&#8217;s distributions </FONT><I><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-LightObl,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>and </FONT></I><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>sold all shares at the end of each period.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=3 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>About Your Fund&#8217;s Expenses</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>As a shareholder of the fund, you incur ongoing costs, which include costs for portfolio management, administrative services, and shareholder reports (like this one), among others. Operating expenses, which are deducted from a fund&#8217;s gross income, directly reduce the investment return of the fund.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>A fund&#8217;s expenses are expressed as a percentage of its average net assets. This figure is known as the expense ratio. The following examples are intended to help you understand the ongoing costs (in dollars) of investing in your fund and to compare these costs with those of other mutual funds. The examples are based on an investment of $1,000 made at the beginning of the period shown and held for the entire period.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The accompanying table illustrates your fund&#8217;s costs in two ways:</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>&#8226; </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Based on actual fund return. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>This section helps you to estimate the actual expenses that you paid over the period. The &#8221;Ending Account Value&#8220; shown is derived from the fund&#8216;s actual return, and the third column shows the dollar amount that would have been paid by an investor who started with $1,000 in the fund. You may use the information here, together with the amount you invested, to estimate the expenses that you paid over the period.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>To do so, simply divide your account value by $1,000 (for example, an $8,600 account value divided by $1,000 = 8.6), then multiply the result by the number given for your fund under the heading &#8221;Expenses Paid During Period.&#8220;</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>&#8226; </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Based on hypothetical 5% yearly return. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>This section is intended to help you compare your fund&#8216;s costs with those of other mutual funds. It assumes that the fund had a yearly return of 5% before expenses, but that the expense ratio is unchanged. In this case&#8212;because the return used is not the fund&#8217;s actual return&#8212;the results do not apply to your investment. The example is useful in making comparisons because the Securities and Exchange Commission requires all mutual funds to calculate expenses based on a 5% return. You can assess your fund&#8217;s costs by comparing this hypothetical example with the hypothetical examples that appear in shareholder reports of other funds.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=Univers-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Note that the expenses shown in the table are meant to highlight and help you compare </FONT><I><FONT size=1 face=Univers-LightOblique,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>ongoing </FONT></I><FONT size=1 face=Univers-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>costs only and do not reflect transaction costs incurred by the fund for buying and selling securities. Further, the expenses do not include any purchase, redemption, or account service fees described in the fund prospectus. If such fees were applied to your account, your costs would be higher. Your fund does not carry a &#8220;sales load.&#8221;</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The calculations assume no shares were bought or sold during the period. Your actual costs may have been higher or lower, depending on the amount of your investment and the timing of any purchases or redemptions.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>You can find more information about the fund&#8217;s expenses, including annual expense ratios, in the Financial Statements section of this report. For additional information on operating expenses and other shareholder costs, please refer to your fund&#8217;s current prospectus.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=3 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Glossary</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>30-Day SEC Yield. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>A fund&#8217;s 30-day SEC yield is derived using a formula specified by the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission. Under the formula, data related to the fund&#8217;s security holdings in the previous 30 days are used to calculate the fund&#8217;s hypothetical net income for that period, which is then annualized and divided by the fund&#8217;s estimated average net assets over the calculation period. For the purposes of this calculation, a security&#8217;s income is based on its current market yield to maturity (for bonds), its actual income (for asset-backed securities), or its projected dividend yield (for stocks). Because the SEC yield represents hypothetical annualized income, it will differ&#8212;at times significantly&#8212;from the fund&#8217;s actual experience. As a result, the fund&#8217;s income distributions may be higher or lower than implied by the SEC yield.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Beta. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>A measure of the magnitude of a fund&#8217;s past share-price fluctuations in relation to the ups and downs of a given market index. The index is assigned a beta of 1.00. Compared with a given index, a fund with a beta of 1.20 typically would have seen its share price rise or fall by 12% when the index rose or fell by 10%. For this report, beta is based on returns over the past 36 months for both the fund and the index. Note that a fund&#8217;s beta should be reviewed in conjunction with its R-squared (see definition). The lower the R-squared, the less correlation there is between the fund and the index, and the less reliable beta is as an indicator of volatility.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Dividend Yield. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Dividend income earned by stocks, expressed as a percentage of the aggregate market value (or of net asset value, for a fund). The yield is determined by dividing the amount of the annual dividends by the aggregate value (or net asset value) at the end of the period. For a fund, the dividend yield is based solely on stock holdings and does not include any income produced by other investments.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Earnings Growth Rate. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The average annual rate of growth in earnings over the past five years for the stocks now in a fund.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Equity Exposure. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>A measure that reflects a fund&#8217;s investments in stocks and stock futures. Any holdings in short-term reserves are excluded.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Expense Ratio. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>A fund&#8217;s total annual operating expenses expressed as a percentage of the fund&#8217;s average net assets. The expense ratio includes management and administrative expenses, but does not include the transaction costs of buying and selling portfolio securities.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Foreign Holdings. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The percentage of a fund represented by securities or depositary receipts of companies based outside the United States.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Inception Date. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The date on which the assets of a fund (or one of its share classes) are first invested in accordance with the fund&#8217;s investment objective. For funds with a subscription period, the inception date is the day after that period ends. Investment performance is measured from the inception date.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Median Market Cap. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>An indicator of the size of companies in which a fund invests; the midpoint of market capitalization (market price x shares outstanding) of a fund&#8217;s stocks, weighted by the proportion of the fund&#8217;s assets invested in each stock. Stocks representing half of the fund&#8217;s assets have market capitalizations above the median, and the rest are below it.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Price/Book Ratio. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The share price of a stock divided by its net worth, or book value, per share. For a fund, the weighted average price/book ratio of the stocks it holds.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>35</FONT></P></DIV>

<DIV style="PAGE-BREAK-BEFORE: always">&nbsp;</DIV>

<!--$$/page=--><A name="page_367"></A><BR>

<DIV style=" PADDING-LEFT: 0%; PADDING-RIGHT: 0%">

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Price/Earnings Ratio. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The ratio of a stock&#8217;s current price to its per-share earnings over the past year. For a fund, the weighted average P/E of the stocks it holds. P/E is an indicator of market expectations about corporate prospects; the higher the P/E, the greater the expectations for a company&#8217;s future growth.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>R-Squared. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>A measure of how much of a fund&#8217;s past returns can be explained by the returns from the market in general, as measured by a given index. If a fund&#8217;s total returns were precisely synchronized with an index&#8217;s returns, its R-squared would be 1.00. If the fund&#8217;s returns bore no relationship to the index&#8217;s returns, its R-squared would be 0. For this report, R-squared is based on returns over the past 36 months for both the fund and the index.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Return on Equity. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The annual average rate of return generated by a company during the past five years for each dollar of shareholder&#8217;s equity (net income divided by shareholder&#8217;s equity). For a fund, the weighted average return on equity for the companies whose stocks it holds.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Short-Term Reserves. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>The percentage of a fund invested in highly liquid, short-term securities that can be readily converted to cash.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Turnover Rate. </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>An indication of the fund&#8217;s trading activity. Funds with high turnover rates incur higher transaction costs and may be more likely to distribute capital gains (which may be taxable to investors). The turnover rate excludes in-kind transactions, which have minimal impact on costs.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=2 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Benchmark Information</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left"><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Spliced Total Stock Market Index: </FONT><FONT size=1 face=UniversLTStd-Light,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif>Dow Jones U.S. Total Stock Market Index (formerly known as the Dow Jones Wilshire 5000 Index) through April 22, 2005; MSCI US Broad Market Index through June 2, 2013; and CRSP US Total Market Index thereafter.</FONT></P>

<P style="text-align: left;">
<B><FONT size=2 face="Arial-BoldMT,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Item 2</FONT></B><FONT size=2 face="Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">: Code of Ethics. The Registrant has adopted a code of ethics that applies to the Registrant&#146;s principal executive officer, principal financial officer, principal accounting officer or controller or persons performing similar functions. The Code of Ethics was amended during the reporting period covered by this report to make certain technical, non-material changes.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<B><FONT size=2 face="Arial-BoldMT,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Item 3</FONT></B><FONT size=2 face="Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">: Audit Committee Financial Expert. The following members of the Audit Committee have been determined by the Registrant&#146;s Board of Trustees to be Audit Committee Financial Experts serving on its Audit Committee, and to be independent: Rajiv L. Gupta, Amy Gutmann, JoAnn Heffernan Heisen, F. Joseph Loughrey, Mark Loughridge, Scott C. Malpass, and Andr&eacute; F. Perold.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<B><FONT size=2 face="Arial-BoldMT,Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Item 4</FONT></B><FONT size=2 face="Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">: Principal Accountant Fees and Services.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=2 face="Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">(a) Audit Fees.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=2 face="Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">Audit Fees of the Registrant</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">

<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=2 face="Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">(e) (1) Pre-Approval Policies. The policy of the Registrant&#146;s Audit Committee is to consider and, if appropriate, approve before the principal accountant is engaged for such services, all specific audit and non-audit services provided to: the Registrant, other registered investment companies in the Vanguard complex, The Vanguard Group, Inc., and entities controlled by The Vanguard Group, Inc. that provide ongoing services to the Registrant. In making a determination, the Audit Committee considers whether the services are consistent with maintaining the principal accountant&#146;s independence.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<FONT size=2 face="Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">In the event of a contingency situation in which the principal accountant is needed to provide services in between scheduled Audit Committee meetings, the Chairman of the Audit Committee would be called on to consider and, if appropriate, pre-approve audit or permitted non-audit services in an amount sufficient to complete services through the next Audit Committee meeting, and to determine if such services would be consistent with maintaining the accountant&#146;s independence. At the next scheduled Audit Committee meeting, services and fees would be presented to the Audit Committee for formal consideration, and, if appropriate, approval by the entire Audit Committee. The Audit Committee would again consider whether such services and fees are consistent with maintaining the principal accountant&#146;s independence.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<FONT size=2 face="Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">The Registrant&#146;s Audit Committee is informed at least annually of all audit and non-audit services provided by the principal accountant to the Vanguard complex, whether such services are provided to: the Registrant, other registered investment companies in the Vanguard complex, The Vanguard Group, Inc., or other entities controlled by The Vanguard Group, Inc. that provide ongoing services to the Registrant.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;<FONT size=2 face="Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">(2) No percentage of the principal accountant&#146;s fees or services were approved pursuant to the waiver provision of paragraph (c)(7)(i)(C) of Rule 2-01 of Regulation S-X.</FONT></P>
<P style="text-align: left;">
<FONT size=2 face="Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">(f) For the most recent fiscal year, over 50% of the hours worked under the principal accountant&#146;s engagement were </FONT><U><FONT size=2 face="Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">not </FONT></U><FONT size=2 face="Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">performed by persons other than full-time, permanent employees of the principal accountant.</FONT></P>

<P style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; PADDING-LEFT: 0%; PADDING-RIGHT: 0%"><FONT size=2 face="Georgia,Times New Roman,Times,serif">In our opinion, the accompanying statement of net assets investments summary and the related statements of operations and of changes in net assets and the financial highlights (included in Item 1 of this Form N-CSR) and the schedule of investments (included in Item 6 of this Form N-CSR) present fairly, in all material respects, the financial position of Vanguard Total Stock Market Index Fund (constituting a separate portfolio of Vanguard Index Funds, hereafter referred to as the &#8220;Fund&#8221;) at December 31, 2015, the results of its operations for the year then ended, the changes in its net assets for each of the two years in the period then ended, and the financial highlights for each of the periods indicated, in conformity with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America. These financial statements, financial highlights, and schedule of investments (hereafter referred to as "financial statements") are the responsibility of the Fund's management. Our responsibility is to express an opinion on these financial statements based on our audits. We conducted our audits of these financial statements in accordance with the standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States). Those standards require that we plan and perform the audit to obtain reasonable assurance about whether the financial statements are free of material misstatement. An audit includes examining, on a test basis, evidence supporting the amounts and disclosures in the financial statements, assessing the accounting principles used and significant estimates made by management, and evaluating the overall financial statement presentation. We believe that our audits, which included confirmation of securities at December 31, 2015 by correspondence with the custodian and brokers, by agreement to the underlying ownership records of the transfer agent and the application of alternative auditing procedures where securities purchased had not been received, provide a reasonable basis for our opinion.</FONT></P>

<p align=right style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:right;"><b><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;text-transform:uppercase;">&nbsp;</font></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:center;"><b><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;text-transform:uppercase;">the
vanguard FUNDS&#8217;</font></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:center;"><b><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;text-transform:uppercase;">CODE OF
Ethics</font></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:center;"><b><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;text-transform:uppercase;">fOR</font></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:center;"><b><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;text-transform:uppercase;">SENIOR
executive and FINANCIAL OFFICERS</font></b></p>

<h1 style="margin-bottom:12.0pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:12.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:0in;"><b><font face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">I.</font></b><b><font face="times new roman" style="font-size:7.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
</font></b><b><font face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">Introduction</font></b></h1>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#160;The Board of
Trustees of each registered investment company that is managed, sponsored, and
distributed by The Vanguard Group, Inc. (&#8220;VGI&#8221;) (each a &#8220;Vanguard Fund&#8221; and
collectively the &#8220;Vanguard Funds&#8221;) has adopted this code of ethics (the &#8220;Code&#8221;)
as required by Section 406 of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act.&#160; The Code applies to the
individuals in positions listed on Exhibit A (the &#8220;Covered Officers&#8221;).&#160; All
Covered Officers, along with employees of The Vanguard Group, Inc., are subject
to separate and distinct obligations from this Code under a Code of Ethics
adopted pursuant to Rule 17j-1 under the Investment Company Act of 1940 (&#8220;17j-1
Code of Ethics&#8221;), policies to prevent the misuse of non-public information, and
other internal compliance guidelines and policies that may be in effect from
time to time.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:6.0pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:12.0pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">This Code is designed to
promote:</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:6.0pt;margin-left:.5in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face=symbol lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#183;</font><font face="times new roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">Honest and ethical conduct, including the ethical handling of
conflicts of interest;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:6.0pt;margin-left:.5in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face=symbol lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#183;</font><font face="times new roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">Full, fair, accurate, timely, and understandable disclosure in
reports and documents that a Vanguard Fund files with, or submits to, the U.S.
Securities and Exchange Commission, or in other public communications made by
the Vanguard Funds or VGI; </font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:6.0pt;margin-left:.5in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face=symbol lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#183;</font><font face="times new roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">Compliance with applicable laws, governmental rules, and
regulations; </font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:6.0pt;margin-left:.5in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face=symbol lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#183;</font><font face="times new roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">Prompt internal reporting to those identified in the Code of
violations of the Code; and</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:6.0pt;margin-left:.5in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face=symbol lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#183;</font><font face="times new roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">Accountability for adherence to the Code.</font></p>

<h1 style="margin-bottom:12.0pt;margin-left:.5in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:12.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-.5in;"><b><font face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">II.</font></b><b><font face="times new roman" style="font-size:7.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
</font></b><b><font face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">Actual or Apparent Conflicts of Interest</font></b></h1>

<h1 style="margin-bottom:12.0pt;margin-left:.5in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:12.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;font-weight:normal;">A.&#160; Covered Officers should
conduct all activities in accordance with the following principles:</font></h1>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;letter-spacing:-.1pt;">1.&#160;&#160; </font><u><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;letter-spacing:-.1pt;">Shareholders&#8217; interests come first</font></u><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;letter-spacing:-.1pt;">. In
the course of fulfilling their duties and responsibilities to Vanguard Fund
shareholders, Covered Officers must at all times place the interests of
Vanguard Fund shareholders first.&#160; In particular, Covered Officers must avoid
serving their own personal interests ahead of the interests of Vanguard Fund
shareholders.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;letter-spacing:-.1pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;letter-spacing:-.1pt;">2.&#160;&#160; </font><u><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;letter-spacing:-.1pt;">Conflicts of interest must be avoided</font></u><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;letter-spacing:-.1pt;">.&#160;
Covered Officers must avoid any situation involving an actual or potential
conflict of interest or possible impropriety with respect to their duties and
responsibilities to Vanguard Fund shareholders. Covered Officers must disclose
any situation that may present the potential for a conflict of interest to
Vanguard&#8217;s Compliance Department, consistent with the 17j-1 Code of Ethics.</font></p>

<p align=center style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:193.5pt;text-align:center;text-indent:-157.5pt;"><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:10.0pt;letter-spacing:-.1pt;">III.14b.1
</font></p>
<a name="_bclFooter1"></a><DIV>


<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font color=#bfbfbf style=""><font color=#bfbfbf face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:9.0pt;">March 20, 2015</font></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font style=""><font face="Times New Roman" lang=X-NONE style="font-size:8.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></font></p>


</DIV>

<a name="_bclHeader2"></a><DIV>


<div style="">

  </td>

<p align=right style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:right;"><font style=""><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;font-weight:normal;">&nbsp;</font></font></p>


</DIV>


<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;letter-spacing:-.1pt;">3.&#160;&#160; </font><u><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;letter-spacing:-.1pt;">Compromising situations must be avoided</font></u><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;letter-spacing:-.1pt;">.&#160;
Covered Officers must not take advantage of their position of trust and
responsibility.&#160; Covered Officers must avoid any situation that might
compromise or call into question their exercise of full independent judgment in
the best interests of Vanguard Fund shareholders.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;letter-spacing:-.1pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;letter-spacing:-.1pt;">All
activities of Covered Officers should be guided by and adhere to these
fiduciary standards regardless of whether the activity is specifically
described in this Code.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-indent:.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">B.&#160; Restricted
Activities</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;letter-spacing:-.1pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;letter-spacing:-.1pt;">1.&#160;&#160; </font><u><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;letter-spacing:-.1pt;">Prohibition on secondary employment</font></u><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;letter-spacing:-.1pt;">.&#160;
Covered Officers are prohibited from accepting or serving in any form of
secondary employment.&#160; Secondary employment that does not create a potential
conflict of interest may be approved by the General Counsel of VGI.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;letter-spacing:-.1pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;letter-spacing:-.1pt;">2.</font><font face="times new roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;letter-spacing:-.1pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
</font><u><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;letter-spacing:-.1pt;">Prohibition on service as
director or public official</font></u><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;letter-spacing:-.1pt;">.&#160;
Unless approved by the General Counsel of VGI, </font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">Covered Officers are
prohibited from serving on the board of directors of any publicly traded
company or in an official capacity for any federal, state, or local government
(or governmental agency or instrumentality).</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;letter-spacing:-.1pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.75in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;letter-spacing:-.1pt;">3.</font><font face="times new roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;letter-spacing:-.1pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
</font><u><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">Prohibition on misuse of Vanguard time or property</font></u><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">.&#160;
Covered Officers are prohibited from making use of time, equipment, services,
personnel or property of any Vanguard entity for any purposes other than the
performance of their duties and responsibilities in connection with the
Vanguard Funds or other Vanguard-related entities.</font></p>

<h1 style="margin-bottom:12.0pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:12.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:0in;"><b><font face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">III.</font></b><b><font face="times new roman" style="font-size:7.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
</font></b><b><font face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">Disclosure and Compliance</font></b></h1>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.5in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">A.&#160; Each
Covered Officer should be familiar with the disclosure requirements generally
applicable to the Vanguard Funds.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.5in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.5in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">B.&#160; Each
Covered Officer should not knowingly misrepresent, or cause others to
misrepresent, facts about the Vanguard Funds to others, including to the
Vanguard Funds&#8217; directors and auditors, or to government regulators and
self-regulatory organizations.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.5in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.5in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">C.&#160; Each
Covered Officer should, to the extent appropriate within the Covered Officer&#8217;s
area of responsibility, consult with other officers and employees of VGI and
advisers to a Vanguard Fund with the goal of promoting full, fair, accurate,
timely and understandable disclosure in the reports and documents the fund
files with, or submits to, the SEC and in other public communications made by a
Vanguard Fund.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.5in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.5in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">D.&#160; It
is the responsibility of each Covered Officer to promote compliance with the
standards and restrictions imposed by applicable laws, rules, regulations, and
the 17j-1 Code of Ethics.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.5in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<h1 style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:0in;">&nbsp;</h1>
<a name="_bclFooter2"></a><DIV>


<p align=center style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:center;"><font face="Times New Roman" lang=X-NONE style="font-size:10.0pt;">III.14b.</font><font style="display:none;"><font face="Times New Roman" lang=X-NONE style="font-size:10.0pt;"></font></font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=X-NONE style="font-size:10.0pt;">2</font><font style="display:none;"><font face="Times New Roman" lang=X-NONE style="font-size:10.0pt;"></font></font></p>

<p align=center style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:center;"><font face="Times New Roman" lang=X-NONE style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align=right style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-align:right;"><font style=""><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;font-weight:normal;">&nbsp;</font></font></p>


</DIV>
<h1 style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:0in;"><b><font face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">IV.</font></b><b><font face="times new roman" style="font-size:7.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
</font></b><b><font face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">Reporting and Accountability</font></b></h1>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">A.&#160; Each
Covered Officer must:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.75in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:13.0pt;">1.</font><font face="times new roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">Upon
adoption or amendment of the Code (or thereafter as applicable, upon becoming a
Covered Officer), affirm in writing that he or she has received, read, and
understands the Code; </font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.75in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-indent:0in;"><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.75in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:13.0pt;">2.</font><font face="times new roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">Affirm
at least annually in writing that he or she has complied with the requirements of
the Code;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-indent:0in;"><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.75in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:13.0pt;">3.</font><font face="times new roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">Not
retaliate against any other Covered Officer or any employee of VGI for reports
of potential violations of the Code that are made in good faith; and</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.75in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-indent:0in;"><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.75in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:13.0pt;">4.</font><font face="times new roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">Notify
the General Counsel of VGI promptly if the Covered Officer knows of any
violations of this Code.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:6.0pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-indent:0in;"><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">B.&#160; The Vanguard Funds will use the following procedures in investigating
and enforcing this Code:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;"><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<h3 style="margin-bottom:12.0pt;margin-left:.75in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:13.0pt;font-weight:normal;">1.</font><font face="times new roman" style="font-size:7.0pt;font-weight:normal;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </font><font face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;font-weight:normal;">The
General Counsel of VGI is responsible for applying this Code to specific
situations and has the authority to interpret this Code in any particular
situation.&#160; The General Counsel will report on an as-needed basis to the Board
of Trustees regarding activities subject to the Code.&#160; </font></h3>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.75in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:13.0pt;">2.</font><font face="times new roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">The
General Counsel will take all appropriate action to investigate any potential
violations of the Code that are reported to him or her.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.5in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;"><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.75in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:13.0pt;">3.</font><font face="times new roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">If,
after investigation, the General Counsel believes that no material violation of
the Code has occurred, the General Counsel is not required to take any further
action.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.75in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:13.0pt;">4.</font><font face="times new roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">Any
matter that the General Counsel believes is a material violation of the Code
will be reported to the Chief Compliance Officer and the Board of Trustees of
the Vanguard Funds.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.5in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-indent:0in;"><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.75in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:13.0pt;">5.</font><font face="times new roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">If
the Board of Trustees of the Vanguard Funds concurs that a material violation
of the Code has occurred, the Board will consider appropriate action.&#160; Appropriate
action may include reassignment, suspension, or dismissal of the applicable
Covered Officer(s), or any other sanctions the Board deems appropriate.&#160; Appropriate
action may also include review of, and appropriate modifications to, applicable
policies and procedures.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.5in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-indent:0in;"><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:.75in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:13.0pt;">6.</font><font face="times new roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:7.0pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; </font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">Any
changes to or waiver of this Code will, to the extent required, be disclosed as
provided by SEC rules.</font></p>

<h1 style="margin-bottom:12.0pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:12.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-indent:0in;"><b><font face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:12.0pt;">Other Policies and Procedures</font></b></h1>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">This Code shall
be the sole code of conduct adopted by the Vanguard Funds for purposes of
Section 406 of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act and the rules and forms applicable to
registered investment companies thereunder. Insofar as other policies or
procedures of the Vanguard Funds, VGI, or other service providers govern or
purport to govern the behavior or activities of the Covered Officers, they are
superseded by this Code to the extent that they overlap or conflict with the
provisions of this Code. </font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in;margin-bottom:.0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font face=timesnewroman lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">VGI&#8217;s and the Vanguard</font><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">
Funds&#8217; 17j-1 Code of Ethics, policies to prevent the misuse of non-public
information, and other internal compliance guidelines and policies that may be
in effect from time to time </font><font face=timesnewroman lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">are
separate requirements applying to the Covered Officers and others, and are not
part of this Code.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:12.0pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:12.0pt;text-indent:0in;"><b><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">VI.&#160; &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; Amendments</font></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:12.0pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:12.0pt;text-indent:0in;"><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; This Code may not be
materially amended except by the approval of a majority vote of the independent
trustees of the Vanguard Funds&#8217; Board of Trustees.&#160; Non-material, technical,
and administrative revisions of the Code do not have to be approved by the
Board of Trustees.&#160;&#160; Amendments must be in writing and communicated promptly to
the Covered Officers, who shall affirm receipt of the amended Code in
accordance with Section IV. A. 1.&#160; </font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:12.0pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:12.0pt;text-indent:0in;"><b><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">VII.&#160; &#160;&#160; Confidentiality</font></b></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:12.0pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:12.0pt;text-indent:0in;"><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; All reports and records
prepared or maintained pursuant to this Code shall be considered confidential
and shall be maintained and protected accordingly.&#160; Except as otherwise
required by law or this Code, such matters shall not be disclosed to anyone
other than </font><font color=black face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">the Vanguard Funds&#8217; Board of Trustees,
VGI&#8217;s General Counsel and the Chief Compliance Officer of VGI and the Vanguard
Funds.</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:12.0pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:12.0pt;text-indent:0in;"><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:12.0pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:12.0pt;text-indent:0in;"><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;">Last Reviewed: March 20, 2015</font></p>

<p style="margin-bottom:.0001pt;margin-left:0in;margin-right:0in;margin-top:0in;text-align:center;"><b><font face="Times New Roman" lang=EN-US style="font-size:12.0pt;text-transform:uppercase;">fOR</font></b></p>
